4.6.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca..
athaibhiḥ pātakairyāṃti yamalokaṃ caturvidhaiḥ..
saṃtrāsajananaṃ ghoraṃ vivaśāḥ sarvadehinaḥ..1..
4.6.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच॥
अथैभिः पातकैर्यांति यमलोकं चतुर्विधैः॥
संत्रासजननं घोरं विवशाः सर्वदेहिनः॥1॥
4.6.m: Glorious Kṛṣṇa said: / Now, on account of these fourfold sins, all embodied beings go, helpless, to the realm of Yama, terrifying and dreadful,

4.6.s:
garbhasthairjāyamānaiśca bālaistaruṇamadhyamaiḥ..
puṃstrīnapuṃsakairvṛddhairjñātavyaṃ sarvajaṃtubhiḥ .. 2 ..
4.6.d:
गर्भस्थैर्जायमानैश्च बालैस्तरुणमध्यमैः॥
पुंस्त्रीनपुंसकैर्वृद्धैर्ज्ञातव्यं सर्वजंतुभिः ॥ 2 ॥
4.6.m: by those in the womb, by those being born, by children, youths, and the middle-aged, / by men, women, eunuchs, and the aged—this must be understood by all living beings.

4.6.s:
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ tatra dehināṃ pravicāryate ..
citraguptādibhiḥ sabhyairmadhyasthaiḥ sarvadarśibhiḥ .. 3 ..
4.6.d:
शुभाशुभफलं तत्र देहिनां प्रविचार्यते ॥
चित्रगुप्तादिभिः सभ्यैर्मध्यस्थैः सर्वदर्शिभिः ॥ 3 ॥
4.6.m: There the auspicious and inauspicious fruit of embodied beings is deliberated upon / by Citragupta and other impartial, all-seeing assembly members.

4.6.s:
na te'tra prāṇinaḥ saṃti ye na yāṃti yamakṣayam ..
avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ tadvidhāritam.. 4 ..
tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaḥ saumyacittā dayānvitāḥ ...8
4.6.d:
न तेऽत्र प्राणिनः संति ये न यांति यमक्षयम् ॥
अवश्यं हि कृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं तद्विधारितम्॥ 4 ॥
तत्र ये शुभकर्माणः सौम्यचित्ता दयान्विताः ॥.8
4.6.m:
There are no living creatures here who do not go to Yama’s abode; / for the action performed must inevitably be experienced as determined by him.
There, those whose deeds are auspicious, whose minds are gentle, who are endowed with compassion,

4.6.s: te narā yāṃti saumyena pathā yamaniketanam .. 5 ..
4.6.d: ते नरा यांति सौम्येन पथा यमनिकेतनम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.6.m: those men go by a gentle path to Yama's dwelling.

4.6.s:
yaḥ pradadyāddvijendrāṇāmupānatkāṣṭhapādukām ..
sa varāśvena mahatā sukhaṃ yāti yamālayam ..6..
4.6.d:
यः प्रदद्याद्द्विजेन्द्राणामुपानत्काष्ठपादुकाम् ॥
स वराश्वेन महता सुखं याति यमालयम् ॥6॥
4.6.m: He who gives shoes and wooden sandals to noble twice-born men / goes comfortably to Yama’s abode upon an excellent, mighty horse.

4.6.s:
chatradānena gacchaṃti yathā chatreṇa dehinaḥ ..
divyavastraparīdhānā yāṃti vastrapradāyinaḥ .. 7 ..
4.6.d:
छत्रदानेन गच्छंति यथा छत्रेण देहिनः ॥
दिव्यवस्त्रपरीधाना यांति वस्त्रप्रदायिनः ॥ 7 ॥
4.6.m: Embodied beings go as if beneath a parasol through the gift of a parasol; / givers of clothing go clad in divine garments.

4.6.s:
śibikāśvapradānena tatastena sukhaṃ vrajet ..
śayyāsana pradānena sukhaṃ yāṃti yamāśrayam .. 8 ..
4.6.d:
शिबिकाश्वप्रदानेन ततस्तेन सुखं व्रजेत् ॥
शय्यासन प्रदानेन सुखं यांति यमाश्रयम् ॥ 8 ॥
4.6.m: By the gift of a palanquin or a horse, one then travels comfortably upon it; / by the gift of a bed or a seat, they go comfortably to Yama’s retreat.

4.6.s:
ārāmakartā chāyāsu śītalāsu sukhaṃ vrajet ..
yāṃti puṣpakayānena puṣpārāmapradāyinaḥ .. 9 ..
4.6.d:
आरामकर्ता छायासु शीतलासु सुखं व्रजेत् ॥
यांति पुष्पकयानेन पुष्पारामप्रदायिनः ॥ 9 ॥
4.6.m: The maker of a grove travels comfortably in cool shade; / givers of flower gardens go in the Puṣpaka vehicle.

4.6.s:
devāyatanakartā ca yatīnāmāśramasya ca ..
anāthamaṃḍapānāṃ ca krīḍanyāti gṛhottamaiḥ .. 4.6.10 ..
4.6.d:
देवायतनकर्ता च यतीनामाश्रमस्य च ॥
अनाथमंडपानां च क्रीडन्याति गृहोत्तमैः ॥ 4.6.10 ॥
4.6.m: A builder of a temple of a deity, of a hermitage for ascetics, / and of pavilions for the destitute travels sportively in excellent mansions.

4.6.s:
devāgniguruviprāṇāṃ mātāpitrośca pūjakāḥ ..
pūjyamānā narā yāṃti kāmikena pathā sukham .. 11 ..
4.6.d:
देवाग्निगुरुविप्राणां मातापित्रोश्च पूजकाः ॥
पूज्यमाना नरा यांति कामिकेन पथा सुखम् ॥ 11 ॥
4.6.m: Worshippers of the gods, the sacred fire, the guru, brahmins, and mother and father / go comfortably by a path that fulfills all desires, being worshipped themselves.

4.6.s:
dyotayaṃto diśaḥ sarvā yāṃti dīpapradāyinaḥ ..
pratiśrayapradānena sukhaṃ yāṃti gṛhaṃ svayam .. 12 ..
4.6.d:
द्योतयंतो दिशः सर्वा यांति दीपप्रदायिनः ॥
प्रतिश्रयप्रदानेन सुखं यांति गृहं स्वयम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.6.m: Givers of lamps go illuminating all the directions; / by the gift of shelter, they go comfortably to [his] home on their own.

4.6.s:
sarva kāmasamṛddhena pathā gacchaṃti gopradāḥ ..
ye na pāpāni kurvaṃti te tṛptā yāṃti nānyathā ..13..
4.6.d:
सर्व कामसमृद्धेन पथा गच्छंति गोप्रदाः ॥
ये न पापानि कुर्वंति ते तृप्ता यांति नान्यथा ॥13॥
4.6.m: Givers of cows travel by a path abounding in all desires; / those who commit no sins go contented, not otherwise.

4.6.s:
ārtauṣadhapradātāraḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti nirākulāḥ ..
viśrāmyamāṇā gacchaṃti guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ..14..
4.6.d:
आर्तौषधप्रदातारः सुखं यांति निराकुलाः ॥
विश्राम्यमाणा गच्छंति गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः॥14॥
4.6.m: Givers of medicine to the sick go comfortably and untroubled; / those devoted to serving their guru go being rested along the way.

4.6.s:
pādaśaucapradānena śītalena pathā vrajet ..
pādābhyaṃgaṃ ca yaḥ kuryādaśvapṛṣṭhena sa vrajet..15..
4.6.d:
पादशौचप्रदानेन शीतलेन पथा व्रजेत् ॥
पादाभ्यंगं च यः कुर्यादश्वपृष्ठेन स व्रजेत्॥15॥
4.6.m: By providing water for washing feet, one travels along a cool path; / and he who performs anointing of the feet travels on horseback.

4.6.s:
hemaratnapradānena yāti durgāṇi nistaran ..
yānavāhanadānena narayānena gacchati .. 16 ..
4.6.d:
हेमरत्नप्रदानेन याति दुर्गाणि निस्तरन् ॥
यानवाहनदानेन नरयानेन गच्छति ॥ 16 ॥
4.6.m: By the gift of gold and jewels, one goes crossing over difficulties; / by the gift of conveyances and mounts, one goes in a palanquin borne by men.

4.6.s:
sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā bhūmidānena gacchati ..
annapānapradānena pibankhādaṃśca gacchati .. 17 ..
4.6.d:
सर्वकामसमृद्धात्मा भूमिदानेन गच्छति ॥
अन्नपानप्रदानेन पिबन्खादंश्च गच्छति ॥ 17 ॥
4.6.m: By the gift of land, one goes with a self enriched with all desires; / by the gift of food and drink, one goes drinking and eating.

4.6.s:
ityevamādibhirdānaiḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti yamakṣayam ..
svargepi vipulānbhogānprāpnuvaṃti narottama .. 18 ..
4.6.d:
इत्येवमादिभिर्दानैः सुखं यांति यमक्षयम् ॥
स्वर्गेपि विपुलान्भोगान्प्राप्नुवंति नरोत्तम ॥ 18 ॥
4.6.m: Through gifts such as these, they go comfortably to Yama’s abode; / and in heaven too they obtain vast enjoyments, O best of men!

4.6.s:
sarveṣāmeva dānānāmannadānaṃ paraṃ smṛtam ..
sadyaḥ prītikaraṃ divyaṃ balabuddhivivarddhanam .. 19 ..
4.6.d:
सर्वेषामेव दानानामन्नदानं परं स्मृतम् ॥
सद्यः प्रीतिकरं दिव्यं बलबुद्धिविवर्द्धनम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.6.m: Among all gifts indeed, the gift of food is considered supreme; / it gives immediate delight, is divine, and increases strength and intellect.

4.6.s:
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ jīvitaṃ hyudakaṃ smṛtam ..
pavitramamṛtaṃ divyaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvarasāyanam .. 4.6.20 ..
4.6.d:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां जीवितं ह्युदकं स्मृतम् ॥
पवित्रममृतं दिव्यं शुद्धं सर्वरसायनम् ॥ 4.6.20 ॥
4.6.m: Water is considered the very life of the three worlds; / it is pure, an elixir, divine, clean, and an elixir of all tastes.

4.6.s:
annaṃ pānaṃ ca govastrabhūśayyācchatramāsanam ..
paraloke praśastāni dānānyaṣṭau viśeṣataḥ .. 21 ..
4.6.d:
अन्नं पानं च गोवस्त्रभूशय्याच्छत्रमासनम् ॥
परलोके प्रशस्तानि दानान्यष्टौ विशेषतः ॥ 21 ॥
4.6.m: Food, drink, a cow, clothing, land, a bed, a parasol, and a seat— / these eight gifts in particular are praised for the other world.

4.6.s:
annadānaṃ viśeṣeṇa dharma rājapure narāḥ ..
yasmādyāṃti sukhenaiva tasmāddharmaṃ samācaret .. 22 ..
4.6.d:
अन्नदानं विशेषेण धर्म राजपुरे नराः ॥
यस्माद्यांति सुखेनैव तस्माद्धर्मं समाचरेत् ॥ 22 ॥
4.6.m: Since, through the gift of food in particular, men go with ease / to the city of Dharmarāja, one should therefore practice righteousness.

4.6.s:
ye punaḥ krūrakarmāṇaḥ pāpā dānavivarjitāḥ ..
te ghoreṇa pathā yāṃti dakṣiṇena svamālayam .. 23 ..
4.6.d:
ये पुनः क्रूरकर्माणः पापा दानविवर्जिताः ॥
ते घोरेण पथा यांति दक्षिणेन स्वमालयम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.6.m: Those, on the other hand, who are of cruel deeds, sinful, and destitute of charity, / go by a dreadful southern path to their own abode,

4.6.s:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāmatītya yat ..
vaivasvatapuraṃ jñeyaṃ nānārūpavyavasthitam .. 24 ..
4.6.d:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानामतीत्य यत् ॥
वैवस्वतपुरं ज्ञेयं नानारूपव्यवस्थितम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.6.m: beyond eighty-six thousand yojanas, where lies / the city of Vaivasvata, known to exist in various forms.

4.6.s:
samīpasthamivābhāti narāṇāṃ śubhakarmaṇām ..
pāpānāmatidūrasthaṃ pathā raudreṇa gacchatām .. 25 ..
4.6.d:
समीपस्थमिवाभाति नराणां शुभकर्मणाम् ॥
पापानामतिदूरस्थं पथा रौद्रेण गच्छताम् ॥ 25 ॥
4.6.m: It appears as if nearby to men of auspicious deeds, / but extremely distant to the sinful who travel by a terrifying path,

4.6.s:
tīvrakaṃṭakayuktena śarkarānicitena ca ..
kṣuradhārānibhaistīvraiḥ pāṣāṇairnicitena ca .. 26 ..
4.6.d:
तीव्रकंटकयुक्तेन शर्करानिचितेन च ॥
क्षुरधारानिभैस्तीव्रैः पाषाणैर्निचितेन च ॥ 26 ॥
4.6.m: filled with sharp thorns, strewn with gravel, / and covered with sharp stones resembling the edges of razors,

4.6.s:
kvacitpaṃkena mahatā duruttāraiśca khātakaiḥ ..
lohasūcīnibhairdarbhaiḥ saṃchannena pathā kvacit .. 27 ..
4.6.d:
क्वचित्पंकेन महता दुरुत्तारैश्च खातकैः ॥
लोहसूचीनिभैर्दर्भैः संछन्नेन पथा क्वचित् ॥ 27 ॥
4.6.m: in some places with deep mud and ditches difficult to cross, / and in some places by a path blanketed with kuśa grass resembling iron needles,

4.6.s:
taṭaprapātaviṣṭaṃbhaiḥ parvatairvṛkṣasaṃkulaiḥ ..
prataptāṃgārayuktena yāṃti mārgeṇa duḥkhitāḥ .. 28 ..
4.6.d:
तटप्रपातविष्टंभैः पर्वतैर्वृक्षसंकुलैः ॥
प्रतप्तांगारयुक्तेन यांति मार्गेण दुःखिताः ॥ 28 ॥
4.6.m: with precipitous cliffs and obstacles, mountains crowded with trees, / [and] along a road covered with glowing embers they travel in misery,

4.6.s:
kvacidviṣamagartaiśca kvacilloṣṭaiḥ supicchilaiḥ ..
prataptavālukābhiśca tathā tīkṣṇaiśca śaṃkubhiḥ .. 29 ..
4.6.d:
क्वचिद्विषमगर्तैश्च क्वचिल्लोष्टैः सुपिच्छिलैः ॥
प्रतप्तवालुकाभिश्च तथा तीक्ष्णैश्च शंकुभिः ॥ 29 ॥
4.6.m: in some places with uneven pits, in some with very slippery clods of earth, / with scorching sands, and likewise with sharp stakes,

4.6.s:
anekatāpairvitatairvyāptaṃ vaṃśavanaṃ kvacit ..
kvacidvālukayā vyāptaṃ kaṣṭenaiva praveśanam .. 4.6.30 ..
4.6.d:
अनेकतापैर्विततैर्व्याप्तं वंशवनं क्वचित् ॥
क्वचिद्वालुकया व्याप्तं कष्टेनैव प्रवेशनम् ॥ 4.6.30 ॥
4.6.m: in some places a bamboo forest spread out, beset by manifold fires, / in some places covered in sand where entrance is gained only with great hardship,

4.6.s:
kvaciduṣṇāṃbunā vyāptaṃ kvacitkārīṣavahninā ..
kvacitsiṃhairvṛkairvyāptaṃ daṃśaiḥ kīṭaiśca dāruṇaiḥ .. 31 ..
4.6.d:
क्वचिदुष्णांबुना व्याप्तं क्वचित्कारीषवह्निना ॥
क्वचित्सिंहैर्वृकैर्व्याप्तं दंशैः कीटैश्च दारुणैः ॥ 31 ॥
4.6.m: in some places filled with boiling water, in some with fire from dried cow dung, / in some places filled with lions and wolves, with gadflies and fierce insects,

4.6.s:
kvacinmahājalaukābhiḥ kvaciccājagaraiḥ punaḥ ..
makṣikābhiśca raudrābhiḥ kvacitsarpairviṣolbaṇaiḥ .. 32 ..
4.6.d:
क्वचिन्महाजलौकाभिः क्वचिच्चाजगरैः पुनः ॥
मक्षिकाभिश्च रौद्राभिः क्वचित्सर्पैर्विषोल्बणैः ॥ 32 ॥
4.6.m: in some places with giant leeches, and again in some with pythons, / with fearsome flies, and in some places with fiercely venomous snakes,

4.6.s:
mattamātaṃgayūthaiśca balonmattaiḥ pramāthibhiḥ ..
paṃthānamullikhadbhiśca tīkṣṇaśṛṃgairmahāvṛṣaiḥ .. 33 ..
4.6.d:
मत्तमातंगयूथैश्च बलोन्मत्तैः प्रमाथिभिः ॥
पंथानमुल्लिखद्भिश्च तीक्ष्णशृंगैर्महावृषैः ॥ 33 ॥
4.6.m: and with herds of rutting elephants, maddened by strength, violent crushers, / and with great bulls with sharp horns that tear up the path,

4.6.s:
mahāviṣāṇairmahiṣairuṣṭrairmattaiśca khādakaiḥ ..
ḍākinībhiśca raudrābhirvikarālaiśca rākṣasaiḥ .. 34 ....
4.6.d:
महाविषाणैर्महिषैरुष्ट्रैर्मत्तैश्च खादकैः ॥
डाकिनीभिश्च रौद्राभिर्विकरालैश्च राक्षसैः ॥ 34 ॥॥
4.6.m: with huge-horned buffaloes, with rutting, man-eating camels, / with terrifying ḍākinīs, and with hideous rākṣasas.

4.6.s:
vyādhibhiśca mahāghoraiḥ pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti ca ..
mahādhūlīvimiśreṇa mahācaṇḍena vāyunā .. 35 ..
4.6.d:
व्याधिभिश्च महाघोरैः पीड्यमाना व्रजंति च ॥
महाधूलीविमिश्रेण महाचण्डेन वायुना ॥ 35 ॥
4.6.m: Tormented by terrible diseases, they travel onward, / and by a fiercely violent wind mixed with great clouds of dust,

4.6.s:
mahāpāṣāṇavarṣeṇa hanyamānā nirāśrayāḥ ..
kvacidvidyutprapātena dīryamāṇā vrajaṃti ca .. 36 ..
4.6.d:
महापाषाणवर्षेण हन्यमाना निराश्रयाः ॥
क्वचिद्विद्युत्प्रपातेन दीर्यमाणा व्रजंति च ॥ 36 ॥
4.6.m: struck by a rain of huge stones, shelterless, / and in some places torn apart by lightning strikes, they travel on,

4.6.s:
mahatā bāṇavarṣeṇa vidhyamānāśca sarvaśaḥ ..
patadbhirvajrasaṃghātairulkāpātaiśca dāruṇaiḥ .. 37 ..
4.6.d:
महता बाणवर्षेण विध्यमानाश्च सर्वशः ॥
पतद्भिर्वज्रसंघातैरुल्कापातैश्च दारुणैः ॥ 37 ॥
4.6.m: pierced on all sides by a mighty shower of arrows, / by falling clusters of thunderbolts, and by dread meteor showers,

4.6.s:
prataptāgāravarṣeṇa dahyamānā vrajaṃti ca ..
taptena pāṃśuvarṣeṇa pūryamāṇā rudaṃti ca .. 38 ..
4.6.d:
प्रतप्तागारवर्षेण दह्यमाना व्रजंति च ॥
तप्तेन पांशुवर्षेण पूर्यमाणा रुदंति च ॥ 38 ॥
4.6.m: burned by a rain of glowing embers, they travel on, / and, covered by a shower of hot dust, they weep.

4.6.s:
mahāmegharavairghorairvitrāsyaṃte muhurmuhuḥ ..
niśitāyudhavarṣeṇa cūryamāṇā narairvṛtāḥ ..
mahākṣārāmbudhārābhiḥ sicyamānā dravaṃti ca .. 39 ..
4.6.d:
महामेघरवैर्घोरैर्वित्रास्यंते मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
निशितायुधवर्षेण चूर्यमाणा नरैर्वृताः ॥
महाक्षाराम्बुधाराभिः सिच्यमाना द्रवंति च ॥ 39 ॥
4.6.m: They are constantly terrified by the dreadful roars of great storm-clouds, / pulverized by a shower of sharp weapons while surrounded by men, / and they flee while being drenched with great streams of caustic water.

4.6.s:
mahāśītena marutā tīkṣṇena paruṣeṇa ca ..
samaṃtātpīḍyamānāste śuṣyaṃte saṃkucaṃti ca .. 4.6.40 ..
4.6.d:
महाशीतेन मरुता तीक्ष्णेन परुषेण च ॥
समंतात्पीड्यमानास्ते शुष्यंते संकुचंति च ॥ 4.6.40 ॥
4.6.m: Tormented on all sides by an intensely cold, piercing, and harsh wind, / they wither away and shrink.

4.6.s:
itthaṃ mārgeṇa raudreṇa pāṃthairvi rahitena ca ..
nirālaṃbena durgeṇa nirjalena samaṃtataḥ ..41..
4.6.d:
इत्थं मार्गेण रौद्रेण पांथैर्वि रहितेन च ॥
निरालंबेन दुर्गेण निर्जलेन समंततः ॥41॥
4.6.m: Along such a terrible path, devoid of travelers, / without support, impassable, and waterless on all sides,

4.6.s:
aviśrāmeṇa mahatā nirgatāpāśrayeṇa ca ..
tamorūpeṇa kaṣṭena sarvaduḥkhāśrayeṇa ca..42..
4.6.d:
अविश्रामेण महता निर्गतापाश्रयेण च ॥
तमोरूपेण कष्टेन सर्वदुःखाश्रयेण च॥42॥
4.6.m: unrelenting, vast, devoid of shelter, / dark in form, distressing, and an abode of all misery—

4.6.s:
nīyaṃte dehinaḥ sarve ye mūḍhāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ ..
yamadūtairmahāghoraistadājñākāribhirbalāt ..43..
4.6.d:
नीयंते देहिनः सर्वे ये मूढाः पापकर्मिणः ॥
यमदूतैर्महाघोरैस्तदाज्ञाकारिभिर्बलात् ॥43॥
4.6.m: all those embodied beings who were foolish and committed evil deeds / are led by force by the most dreadful messengers of Yama who carry out his commands.

4.6.s:
ekākinaḥ parādhīnā mitrabaṃdhuvivarjitāḥ ..
śocaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi rudaṃtaśca muhurmuhuḥ .. 44 ..
4.6.d:
एकाकिनः पराधीना मित्रबंधुविवर्जिताः ॥
शोचंतः स्वानि कर्माणि रुदंतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 44 ॥
4.6.m: Alone, dependent on others, bereft of friends and relatives, / grieving their own actions and weeping again and again,

4.6.s:
pretabhūtā vivastrāśca śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukāḥ ..
kṛśāṅgā bhītabhītāśca dahyamānāḥ kṣudhāgninā .. 45 ..
4.6.d:
प्रेतभूता विवस्त्राश्च शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुकाः ॥
कृशाङ्गा भीतभीताश्च दह्यमानाः क्षुधाग्निना ॥ 45 ॥
4.6.m: turned into pretas, unclothed, their throats, lips, and palates parched, / emaciated in body, thoroughly terrified, and burning with the fire of hunger,

4.6.s:
baddhāḥ śṛṃkhalayā keciduttānāḥ pādayornarāḥ ..
ākṛṣyaṃte ghṛṣyamāṇā yamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ .. 46 ..
4.6.d:
बद्धाः शृंखलया केचिदुत्तानाः पादयोर्नराः ॥
आकृष्यंते घृष्यमाणा यमदूतैर्बलोत्कटैः ॥ 46 ॥
4.6.m: some men, bound by the feet with a chain, face upward, / are dragged along, scraping against the ground, by the messengers of Yama of formidable strength.

4.6.s:
punaścādhomukhāścānye ghṛṣyamāṇāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ..
keśapāśanibaddhāśca kṛṣyaṃte rajjubhirnarāḥ .. 47 ..
4.6.d:
पुनश्चाधोमुखाश्चान्ये घृष्यमाणाः सुदुःखिताः॥
केशपाशनिबद्धाश्च कृष्यंते रज्जुभिर्नराः ॥ 47 ॥
4.6.m: Others, facing downward, deeply afflicted, are scraped along; / and men, bound by their braids of hair, are pulled with ropes.

4.6.s:
lalāṭe cāṃkuśaistīkṣṇairbhinnāḥ kṛṣyaṃti dehinaḥ ..
uttānā raṭamānāśca kvacidaṃgāravartmanā.. 48 ..
4.6.d:
ललाटे चांकुशैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भिन्नाः कृष्यंति देहिनः ॥
उत्ताना रटमानाश्च क्वचिदंगारवर्त्मना॥ 48 ॥
4.6.m: Pierced on the forehead with sharp goads, embodied beings are dragged along; / lying on their backs and screaming, in some places along a path of burning coals,

4.6.s:
pāścādbāhvaṃsabaddhāśca jaṭhare ca prapīḍitāḥ ..
pūritāḥ śṛṃkhalābhiśca hastayośca prakīlitāḥ .. 49 ..
4.6.d:
पाश्चाद्बाह्वंसबद्धाश्च जठरे च प्रपीडिताः ॥
पूरिताः शृंखलाभिश्च हस्तयोश्च प्रकीलिताः ॥ 49 ॥
4.6.m: bound behind by their arms and shoulders, squeezed in their bellies, / locked with chains, and pinned down by their hands,

4.6.s:
grīvāyāmarddhacandreṇa kṣipyamāṇā itastataḥ ..
śiśne ca vṛṣaṇe baddhvā nīyaṃte carmarajjunā .. 4.6.50 ..
4.6.d:
ग्रीवायामर्द्धचन्द्रेण क्षिप्यमाणा इतस्ततः ॥
शिश्ने च वृषणे बद्ध्वा नीयंते चर्मरज्जुना ॥ 4.6.50 ॥
4.6.m: flung here and there by a crescent-shaped blade at the neck, / and having their penis and testicles bound with a leather strap, they are led away.

4.6.s:
vibhinnā udare cānye taptaśṛṃkhalayā narāḥ ..
kṛṣyaṃte karṇayoścānye bhinnāśca cibukopari .. .. 51 ..
4.6.d:
विभिन्ना उदरे चान्ये तप्तशृंखलया नराः ॥
कृष्यंते कर्णयोश्चान्ये भिन्नाश्च चिबुकोपरि ॥ ॥ 51 ॥
4.6.m: Other men are pierced in the belly with a glowing chain; / others are dragged by their ears, and pierced above the chin.

4.6.s:
chinnāgrapādahastāśca chinnakarṇauṣṭhanāsikāḥ ..
saṃchinnaśiśnavṛṣaṇāśchinnabhinnāṃgasaṃdhayaḥ .. 52 ..
4.6.d:
छिन्नाग्रपादहस्ताश्च छिन्नकर्णौष्ठनासिकाः ॥
संछिन्नशिश्नवृषणाश्छिन्नभिन्नांगसंधयः ॥ 52 ॥
4.6.m: With the tips of their feet and hands cut off, with ears, lips, and noses severed, / with penises and testicles completely amputated, their joints slashed and pierced,

4.6.s:
pratudyamānāḥ kuṃtaiśca sāyakaiśca tatastataḥ ..
bhidyamānāḥ pradhāvaṃti krandamānā nirāśrayāḥ .. 53 ..
4.6.d:
प्रतुद्यमानाः कुंतैश्च सायकैश्च ततस्ततः ॥
भिद्यमानाः प्रधावंति क्रन्दमाना निराश्रयाः ॥ 53 ॥
4.6.m: prodded here and there with lances and arrows, / pierced through, they run about, crying out, without shelter,

4.6.s:
mudgarairllohadaṇḍaiśca hanyamānā muhurmuhuḥ ..
kaśaiśca vividhaighorairjvalitāgnisamaprabhaiḥ .. 54 ..
4.6.d:
मुद्गरैर्ल्लोहदण्डैश्च हन्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
कशैश्च विविधैघोरैर्ज्वलिताग्निसमप्रभैः ॥ 54 ॥
4.6.m: beaten again and again with clubs and iron rods, / and with various terrible whips resembling blazing fire,

4.6.s:
bhiṃdipālairvibhidyaṃte sravaṃtaḥ pūyaśoṇitam ..
māṃse kṣatāśca kṛmibhirnīyaṃte vivaśā narāḥ .. 55 ..
4.6.d:
भिंदिपालैर्विभिद्यंते स्रवंतः पूयशोणितम् ॥
मांसे क्षताश्च कृमिभिर्नीयंते विवशा नराः ॥ 55 ॥
4.6.m: they are pierced with slings, oozing pus and blood; / their flesh wounded by worms, the helpless men are led away.

4.6.s:
yācamānāśca salilamannaṃ cāpi bubhukṣitāḥ ..
chāyāṃ prārthayamānāśca śītārtā bahuvāyunā .. 56 ..
4.6.d:
याचमानाश्च सलिलमन्नं चापि बुभुक्षिताः ॥
छायां प्रार्थयमानाश्च शीतार्ता बहुवायुना ॥ 56 ॥
4.6.m: Begging for water and for food, famished, / and imploring for shade, shivering from the strong wind,

4.6.s:
dānahīnāḥ prayāṃtyevaṃ yāvaṃto vimukhā narāḥ ..
gṛhītadānapātheyāḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti yamālayam .. 57 ..
4.6.d:
दानहीनाः प्रयांत्येवं यावंतो विमुखा नराः ॥
गृहीतदानपाथेयाः सुखं यांति यमालयम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.6.m: so many men who were devoid of giving go thus, turned away [from virtue]; / those who took the travel-provisions of gifts go happily to the abode of Yama.

4.6.s:
evaṃ pathātikaṣṭena prāptā yamapuraṃ tadā ..
prajñāpitāstadā dūtairniveśyaṃte yamāgrataḥ .. 58 ..
4.6.d:
एवं पथातिकष्टेन प्राप्ता यमपुरं तदा ॥
प्रज्ञापितास्तदा दूतैर्निवेश्यंते यमाग्रतः ॥ 58 ॥
4.6.m: Having thus reached the city of Yama along that most painful path, / announced then by the messengers, they are ushered into the presence of Yama.

4.6.s:
tatra ye śubhakarmāṇastāṃśca saṃmānayedyamaḥ ..
svāgatāsanadānena pādyārgheṇa priyeṇa ca .. 59 ..
4.6.d:
तत्र ये शुभकर्माणस्तांश्च संमानयेद्यमः ॥
स्वागतासनदानेन पाद्यार्घेण प्रियेण च ॥ 59 ॥
4.6.m: There, Yama honors those whose deeds were auspicious / by offering a welcome, a seat, foot-water, arghya, and kind words:

4.6.s:
dhanyā yūyaṃ mahātmāna ātmano hitakāriṇaḥ ..
yena divyasukhārthāya bhavadbhiḥ sukṛtaṃ kṛtam .. 4.6.60 ..
4.6.d:
धन्या यूयं महात्मान आत्मनो हितकारिणः ॥
येन दिव्यसुखार्थाय भवद्भिः सुकृतं कृतम् ॥ 4.6.60 ॥
4.6.m: ‘Blessed are you, great-souled ones, benefactors of yourselves, / by whom good deeds were performed for the sake of divine happiness!

4.6.s:
idaṃ vimānamāruhya divyastrībhogabhūṣitam ..
svargaṃ gacchadhvamatulaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitam .. 61 ..
4.6.d:
इदं विमानमारुह्य दिव्यस्त्रीभोगभूषितम् ॥
स्वर्गं गच्छध्वमतुलं सर्वकामसमन्वितम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.6.m: Having ascended this celestial chariot adorned with the pleasures of heavenly women, / go to peerless heaven, endowed with every desire.

4.6.s:
tato bhuktvā mahābhogānaṃte puṇyasya saṃkṣayāt ..
yatkiñcidalpamaśubhaṃ punastadiha bhokṣyatha .. 62 ..
4.6.d:
ततो भुक्त्वा महाभोगानंते पुण्यस्य संक्षयात् ॥
यत्किञ्चिदल्पमशुभं पुनस्तदिह भोक्ष्यथ ॥ 62 ॥
4.6.m: Then, having enjoyed great pleasures, at the end, through the exhaustion of merit, / whatever little evil there is, you will experience it again here.’

4.6.s:
te cāpi dharmarājānaṃ narāḥ puṇyānubhāvataḥ ..
paśyaṃti saumyavadanaṃ pitṛbhūtamivātmanaḥ .. 63 ..
4.6.d:
ते चापि धर्मराजानं नराः पुण्यानुभावतः ॥
पश्यंति सौम्यवदनं पितृभूतमिवात्मनः ॥ 63 ॥
4.6.m: Those men too, by the power of their merit, / behold Dharmarāja with a gentle face, like a father to them.

4.6.s:
ye punaḥ pāpakarmāṇaste paśyaṃti bhayānakam ..
pāpāviśuddhanayanā viparītātmabuddhayaḥ .. 64 ..
4.6.d:
ये पुनः पापकर्माणस्ते पश्यंति भयानकम् ॥
पापाविशुद्धनयना विपरीतात्मबुद्धयः ॥ 64 ॥
4.6.m: Those, on the other hand, who committed evil deeds, see him as terrifying, / their eyes clouded by sin, their intellects utterly perverted:

4.6.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ bhrukuṭīkuṭilekṣaṇam ..
ūrdhvakeśaṃ mahāśmaśruprasphuradadharottaram .. 65 ..
4.6.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनं भ्रुकुटीकुटिलेक्षणम् ॥
ऊर्ध्वकेशं महाश्मश्रुप्रस्फुरदधरोत्तरम् ॥ 65 ॥
4.6.m: his face dreadful with fangs, his glance crooked with a frown, / his hair standing erect, with a huge beard, his upper and lower lips quivering,

4.6.s:
aṣṭādaśabhujaṃ kruddhaṃ nīlāṃjanacayopamam ..
savāryudhodyatakaraṃ brahmadaṇḍena tarjakam .. 66 ..
4.6.d:
अष्टादशभुजं क्रुद्धं नीलांजनचयोपमम् ॥
सवार्युधोद्यतकरं ब्रह्मदण्डेन तर्जकम् ॥ 66 ॥
4.6.m: eighteen-armed, enraged, resembling a heap of blue collyrium, / his hands raised with all kinds of weapons, threatening with the staff of Brahmā,

4.6.s:
mahāmahiṣamārūḍhaṃ dīptāgnisamalocanam ..
raktamālyāmbaradharaṃ mahāmerumivocchritam .. 67 ..
4.6.d:
महामहिषमारूढं दीप्ताग्निसमलोचनम् ॥
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरं महामेरुमिवोच्छ्रितम् ॥ 67 ॥
4.6.m: mounted upon a great buffalo, his eyes like blazing fire, / wearing red garlands and garments, towering like Mount Meru,

4.6.s:
pralayāṃbudanirghoṣaṃ pibaṃtamiva sāgaram ..
grasaṃtamiva lokānāmudgiraṃtamivānalam .. 68 ..
4.6.d:
प्रलयांबुदनिर्घोषं पिबंतमिव सागरम् ॥
ग्रसंतमिव लोकानामुद्गिरंतमिवानलम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.6.m: roaring like the storm-clouds of cosmic dissolution, seeming to swallow the ocean, / seeming to devour the worlds, seeming to vomit forth fire.

4.6.s:
mṛtyuśca tatsamīpasthaḥ kālānalasamaprabhaḥ ..
kālaścāṃjanasaṃkāśaḥ kṛtāṃtaśca bhayānakaḥ .. 69 ..
4.6.d:
मृत्युश्च तत्समीपस्थः कालानलसमप्रभः ॥
कालश्चांजनसंकाशः कृतांतश्च भयानकः ॥ 69 ॥
4.6.m: And Mṛtyu stands near him, radiant like the fire of destruction, / and Kāla resembling collyrium, and terrifying Kṛtānta,

4.6.s:
mārī cogrā mahāmārī kālarātriḥ sudāruṇā ..
vividhā vyādhayaḥ kaṣṭā nānārūpabhayāvahāḥ .. 4.6.70 ..
4.6.d:
मारी चोग्रा महामारी कालरात्रिः सुदारुणा ॥
विविधा व्याधयः कष्टा नानारूपभयावहाः ॥ 4.6.70 ॥
4.6.m: and fierce Mārī, Mahāmārī, and dreadful Kālarātri, / along with various painful diseases, terrifying in their many forms,

4.6.s:
śaktiśūlāṃkuśadharāḥ pāśacakrāsidhāriṇaḥ ..
vajradaṇḍadharā raudrāḥ kṣudratūṇīdhanurdharāḥ .. 71 ..
4.6.d:
शक्तिशूलांकुशधराः पाशचक्रासिधारिणः ॥
वज्रदण्डधरा रौद्राः क्षुद्रतूणीधनुर्धराः ॥ 71 ॥
4.6.m: holding spears, tridents, and goads, bearing nooses, discs, and swords, / holding thunderbolts and staffs, fierce, carrying small quivers and bows,

4.6.s:
asaṃkhyātā mahāvīryāḥ krūrāścāñjanasaṃprabhāḥ ..
sarvāyudhodyatakarā yamadūtā bhayānakāḥ .. 72 ..
4.6.d:
असंख्याता महावीर्याः क्रूराश्चाञ्जनसंप्रभाः ॥
सर्वायुधोद्यतकरा यमदूता भयानकाः ॥ 72 ॥
4.6.m: innumerable, of great prowess, cruel, shining like collyrium, / the terrifying messengers of Yama, with their hands raised with all weapons.

4.6.s:
anena parivāreṇa mahāghoreṇa saṃvṛtam ..
yamaṃ paśyaṃti pāpiṣṭhāścitraguptaṃ ca bhīṣaṇam ..
nirbhartsayataṃ cātyantaṃ yamaṃ sadupakāriṇam ..73..
4.6.d:
अनेन परिवारेण महाघोरेण संवृतम् ॥
यमं पश्यंति पापिष्ठाश्चित्रगुप्तं च भीषणम् ॥
निर्भर्त्सयतं चात्यन्तं यमं सदुपकारिणम् ॥73॥
4.6.m: Surrounded by this most dreadful retinue, / the wicked see Yama and fearsome Citragupta, / who severely reproaches [them, while honoring] Yama, the benefactor of the virtuous.

4.6.s:
citraguptaśca bhagavāndharmavākyaiḥ prabodhayan ..
bhobho duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ .
garvitā rūpavīryeṇa paradāravimardakāḥ ..74..
4.6.d:
चित्रगुप्तश्च भगवान्धर्मवाक्यैः प्रबोधयन् ॥
भोभो दुष्कृतकर्माणः परद्रव्यापहारिणः ।
गर्विता रूपवीर्येण परदारविमर्दकाः ॥74॥
4.6.m: And the blessed Citragupta, admonishing them with words of righteousness, [says]: / ‘O evil-doers, robbers of others' wealth, / proud of your beauty and prowess, violators of others' wives!

4.6.s:
yatsvayaṃ kriyate karma tatsvayaṃ bhujyate punaḥ ..
tatkimātmopaghātārthaṃ bhavadbhirduṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ..75..
4.6.d:
यत्स्वयं क्रियते कर्म तत्स्वयं भुज्यते पुनः ॥
तत्किमात्मोपघातार्थं भवद्भिर्दुष्कृतं कृतम् ॥75॥
4.6.m: The deed that one does oneself, that very deed one enjoys in return. / Why then did you perform evil for your own destruction?

4.6.s:
idānīṃ kiṃ pratapyadhvaṃ pīḍyamānāḥ svakarmabhiḥ ..
bhuñjadhvaṃ svāni karmāṇi nātra doṣo'sti kasyacit .. 76 ..
4.6.d:
इदानीं किं प्रतप्यध्वं पीड्यमानाः स्वकर्मभिः ॥
भुञ्जध्वं स्वानि कर्माणि नात्र दोषोऽस्ति कस्यचित् ॥ 76 ॥
4.6.m: Why do you now burn with anguish, tormented by your own actions? / Suffer your own deeds; no one else is at fault here.’

4.6.s:
ete ca pṛthivīpālāḥ saṃprāptā matsamīpataḥ ..
svakīyaiḥ karmabhirghorairduṣprajñā balagarvitāḥ .. 77 ..
4.6.d:
एते च पृथिवीपालाः संप्राप्ता मत्समीपतः ॥
स्वकीयैः कर्मभिर्घोरैर्दुष्प्रज्ञा बलगर्विताः ॥ 77 ॥
4.6.m: ‘And these rulers of the earth have arrived in my presence / through their own dreadful deeds, foolish and arrogant in their might.

4.6.s:
bhobho nṛpā durācārāḥ prajāvidhvaṃsakāriṇaḥ ..
alpakālasya rājyasya kṛte kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam .. 78 ..
4.6.d:
भोभो नृपा दुराचाराः प्रजाविध्वंसकारिणः ॥
अल्पकालस्य राज्यस्य कृते किं दुष्कृतं कृतम् ॥ 78 ॥
4.6.m: O kings of evil conduct, destroyers of your subjects! / For the sake of a short-lived sovereignty, why was evil done?

4.6.s:
rājyalobhena mohādvā balādanyāyataḥ prajāḥ ..
yatpīḍitāḥ phalaṃ tasya bhuṃjadhvamadhunā nṛpāḥ .. 79 ..
4.6.d:
राज्यलोभेन मोहाद्वा बलादन्यायतः प्रजाः ॥
यत्पीडिताः फलं तस्य भुंजध्वमधुना नृपाः ॥ 79 ॥
4.6.m: Because through greed for kingdom or through delusion, by force and injustice, your subjects / were oppressed—now, O kings, experience the fruit of that!

4.6.s:
kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kalatraṃ ca yadarthamaśubhaṃ kṛtam ..
tatsarvaṃ saṃparityajya yūyamekākinaḥ sthitāḥ .. 4.6.80 ..
4.6.d:
कृतं राज्यं कलत्रं च यदर्थमशुभं कृतम् ॥
तत्सर्वं संपरित्यज्य यूयमेकाकिनः स्थिताः ॥ 4.6.80 ॥
4.6.m: The kingdom that was won and the wives for whose sake evil was done— / leaving all that behind, you stand alone.

4.6.s:
paśyāma tadbalaṃ tubhyaṃ yena vidhvaṃsitāḥ prajāḥ ..
yamadūtaistāḍyamānā adhunā kīdṛśaṃ bhavet.. 81 ..
4.6.d:
पश्याम तद्बलं तुभ्यं येन विध्वंसिताः प्रजाः ॥
यमदूतैस्ताड्यमाना अधुना कीदृशं भवेत्॥ 81 ॥
4.6.m: Let us see that might of yours by which your subjects were destroyed! / Being struck by the messengers of Yama, what will it be like now?’

4.6.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhairvākyairupālabdhā yamena te ..
śocaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhaṃti pārthiva .. 82 ..
4.6.d:
एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरुपालब्धा यमेन ते ॥
शोचंतः स्वानि कर्माणि तूष्णीं तिष्ठंति पार्थिव ॥ 82 ॥
4.6.m: Thus reproached with diverse words by Yama, / those [kings], grieving over their own deeds, stood in silence, O king.

4.6.s:
iti dharmaṃ samādiśya nṛpāṇāṃ dharmarāṭ punaḥ ..
tatpāpapaṃkaśuddhyarthamidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 83 ..
4.6.d:
इति धर्मं समादिश्य नृपाणां धर्मराट् पुनः ॥
तत्पापपंकशुद्ध्यर्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 83 ॥
4.6.m: Having thus instructed the kings in righteousness, the King of Dharma again / spoke these words to cleanse the mire of their sins:

4.6.s:
bhobhoścaṇḍa mahācaṇḍa gṛhītvā nṛpatīnimān ..
viśodhayadhvaṃ pāpebhyaḥ krameṇa narakāgniṣu ..84..
4.6.d:
भोभोश्चण्ड महाचण्ड गृहीत्वा नृपतीनिमान् ॥
विशोधयध्वं पापेभ्यः क्रमेण नरकाग्निषु ॥84॥
4.6.m: "O Caṇḍa, O Mahācaṇḍa, take hold of these kings, / and cleanse them from their sins by degrees in the hellish fires."

4.6.s:
tataḥ śīghraṃ samutthāya nṛpānsaṃgṛhya pādayoḥ ..
bhrāmayitvātivegena vikṣipyordhvaṃ vigṛhya ca .. 85 ..
4.6.d:
ततः शीघ्रं समुत्थाय नृपान्संगृह्य पादयोः ॥
भ्रामयित्वातिवेगेन विक्षिप्योर्ध्वं विगृह्य च ॥ 85 ॥
4.6.m: Then, rising swiftly and seizing the kings by their feet, / whirling [them] with great speed, hurling [them] upwards and catching [them],

4.6.s:
sarvaprāṇena mahatā sutapte tu śilātale ..
ā sphālayaṃti tarasā vajreṇeva mahādrumam .. 86 ..
4.6.d:
सर्वप्राणेन महता सुतप्ते तु शिलातले ॥
आ स्फालयंति तरसा वज्रेणेव महाद्रुमम् ॥ 86 ॥
4.6.m: with all their great might, upon the thoroughly heated surface of a rock / they dash [them] down violently, like a great tree with a thunderbolt.

4.6.s:
tataḥ sa raktasrotobhiḥ sravate jarjarīkṛtaḥ ..
sa niḥsaṃjñastadā dehī niśceṣṭaḥ saṃprajāyate .. 87 ..
4.6.d:
ततः स रक्तस्रोतोभिः स्रवते जर्जरीकृतः ॥
स निःसंज्ञस्तदा देही निश्चेष्टः संप्रजायते ॥ 87 ॥
4.6.m: Then, shattered, he bleeds with streams of blood; / then that embodied soul becomes unconscious and motionless.

4.6.s:
tataḥ sa vāyunā spṛṣṭaḥ śanairujīvate punaḥ ..
tataḥ pāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṣipyate narakārṇave .. 88 ..
4.6.d:
ततः स वायुना स्पृष्टः शनैरुजीवते पुनः ॥
ततः पापविशुद्ध्यर्थं क्षिप्यते नरकार्णवे ॥ 88 ॥
4.6.m: Then, touched by the wind, he slowly revives again; / then, for the purification of his sins, he is cast into the ocean of hell.

4.6.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatirevādhaḥ kṣiternarakakoṭayaḥ..
saptamasya talasyāṃte ghore tamasi saṃsthitāḥ .. 89 ..
4.6.d:
अष्टाविंशतिरेवाधः क्षितेर्नरककोटयः॥
सप्तमस्य तलस्यांते घोरे तमसि संस्थिताः ॥ 89 ॥
4.6.m: Indeed, twenty-eight crores of hells lie beneath the earth, / stationed in dreadful darkness at the end of the seventh level.

4.6.s:
rauravaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca narakāṇāṃ śataṃ smṛtam ..
catvāriṃśatsamadhikaṃ mahānarakamaṃḍalam .. 4.6.90 ..
4.6.d:
रौरवप्रभृतीनां च नरकाणां शतं स्मृतम् ॥
चत्वारिंशत्समधिकं महानरकमंडलम् ॥ 4.6.90 ॥
4.6.m: And of the hells beginning with Raurava, one hundred and forty / are remembered as the great sphere of hells,

4.6.s:
yeṣu pāpāḥ prapacyaṃte narāḥ karmānurūpataḥ ..
yātanābhirvicitrābhirākarmaprakṣayādbhṛśam .. 91 ..
4.6.d:
येषु पापाः प्रपच्यंते नराः कर्मानुरूपतः ॥
यातनाभिर्विचित्राभिराकर्मप्रक्षयाद्भृशम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.6.m: in which sinful men are cooked according to their deeds / with diverse torments, intensely, until their deeds are exhausted.

4.6.s:
ā malaprakṣayādyadvadagnau dhāsyaṃti dhātavaḥ ..
tathā pāpakṣayātpāpāśśodhyaṃte narakāgniṣu .. 92 ..
4.6.d:
आ मलप्रक्षयाद्यद्वदग्नौ धास्यंति धातवः ॥
तथा पापक्षयात्पापाश्शोध्यंते नरकाग्निषु ॥ 92 ॥
4.6.m: Just as minerals will be held in fire until their dross is destroyed, / even so, until their sins are destroyed, sinners are cleansed in the fires of hell.

4.6.s:
sugāḍhahastayā bāḍhaṃ taptaśṛṃkhalayā narāḥ ..
mahāvṛkṣāgraśākhāyāṃ laṃbyaṃte yamakiṃkaraiḥ .. 93 .. .
4.6.d:
सुगाढहस्तया बाढं तप्तशृंखलया नराः ॥
महावृक्षाग्रशाखायां लंब्यंते यमकिंकरैः ॥ 93 ॥ ।
4.6.m: Men with their hands bound very tightly by red-hot chains / are suspended from the top branch of a great tree by Yama's attendants.

4.6.s:
tataste sarpayaṃtreṇa kṣiptā dolyaṃti kiṃkaraiḥ ..
dolyaṃtaścātivegena niḥsaṃjñā yāṃti yojanam .. 94 ..
4.6.d:
ततस्ते सर्पयंत्रेण क्षिप्ता दोल्यंति किंकरैः ॥
दोल्यंतश्चातिवेगेन निःसंज्ञा यांति योजनम् ॥ 94 ॥
4.6.m: Then, propelled by a serpentine apparatus, they are swung by the attendants; / and being swung with extreme speed, they travel a yojana, senseless.

4.6.s:
aṃtarikṣasthitānāṃ ca lohabhāraśataṃ tataḥ ..
pādayorbadhyate teṣāṃ yamadūtairmahābalaiḥ .. 95 ..
4.6.d:
अंतरिक्षस्थितानां च लोहभारशतं ततः ॥
पादयोर्बध्यते तेषां यमदूतैर्महाबलैः ॥ 95 ॥
4.6.m: And as they hang in mid-air, a weight of a hundred iron [bars] / is then bound to their feet by Yama's mighty messengers.

4.6.s:
tena bhāreṇa mahatā bhṛśamātardditā narāḥ ..
dhyāyaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭheti vihvalāḥ .. ..96 ..
4.6.d:
तेन भारेण महता भृशमातर्द्दिता नराः ॥
ध्यायंतः स्वानि कर्माणि तूष्णीं तिष्ठेति विह्वलाः ॥ ॥96 ॥
4.6.m: Tormented exceedingly by that great weight, / men, meditating upon their own deeds, stay in silence, distraught.

4.6.s:
jvālābhiragnivarṇābhirllohadaṃḍaiḥ sakaṃṭakaiḥ..
hanyaṃte kiṃkarairghoraiḥ samaṃtātpāpakāriṇaḥ ..97 ..
4.6.d:
ज्वालाभिरग्निवर्णाभिर्ल्लोहदंडैः सकंटकैः॥
हन्यंते किंकरैर्घोरैः समंतात्पापकारिणः ॥97 ॥
4.6.m: With iron rods, barbed and glowing like flames of fire, / the evil-doers are struck on all sides by terrible attendants.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena vahnerapi viśeṣataḥ ..
samaṃtataḥ pralipyaṃte kṣatāṃgā jarjarīkṛtāḥ .. 98 ..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन वह्नेरपि विशेषतः ॥
समंततः प्रलिप्यंते क्षतांगा जर्जरीकृताः ॥ 98 ॥
4.6.m: Then, with burning caustic, even more intense than fire, / their wounded limbs, mangled, are smeared all over.

4.6.s:
punarvidārya cāṃgeṣu śirasaḥprabhṛti kramāt ..
vṛntākavatprapacyaṃte taptatailakaṭāhake .. 99 ..
4.6.d:
पुनर्विदार्य चांगेषु शिरसःप्रभृति क्रमात् ॥
वृन्ताकवत्प्रपच्यंते तप्ततैलकटाहके ॥ 99 ॥
4.6.m: Then, torn open again in their limbs successively from the head downwards, / they are cooked like eggplants in a cauldron of boiling oil.

4.6.s:
viṣṭhāpūrṇe tataḥ kūpe kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye tataḥ ..
medastvakpūyapūrṇāyāṃ vāpyāṃ kṣipyaṃti te punaḥ .. 4.6.100 ..
4.6.d:
विष्ठापूर्णे ततः कूपे कृमीणां निचये ततः ॥
मेदस्त्वक्पूयपूर्णायां वाप्यां क्षिप्यंति ते पुनः ॥ 4.6.100 ॥
4.6.m: Then into a pit filled with feces, then into a mass of worms, / and into a reservoir filled with fat, skin, and pus they cast them again.

4.6.s:
bhakṣyaṃte krimibhistīkṣṇairlohatuṇḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ ..
śvabhirdaṃśairvṛkairghorairvyāghrairapyatha vānaraiḥ .. 101 ..
4.6.d:
भक्ष्यंते क्रिमिभिस्तीक्ष्णैर्लोहतुण्डैश्च वायसैः ॥
श्वभिर्दंशैर्वृकैर्घोरैर्व्याघ्रैरप्यथ वानरैः ॥ 101 ॥
4.6.m: They are devoured by fierce worms, by crows with iron beaks, / by dogs, by gadflies, by dreadful wolves, by tigers, and also by monkeys.

4.6.s:
pacyaṃte māṃsavaccāpi pradīptāṃgārarāśiṣu ..
protāḥ śūleṣu tīkṣṇeṣu narāḥ pāpena karmaṇā .. 102..
4.6.d:
पच्यंते मांसवच्चापि प्रदीप्तांगारराशिषु ॥
प्रोताः शूलेषु तीक्ष्णेषु नराः पापेन कर्मणा ॥ 102॥
4.6.m: And impaled on sharp stakes, men through their sinful deed / are cooked like meat upon heaps of blazing coals.

4.6.s:
tilapiṃḍairivākramya ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmanaḥ ..
tilavatsamprapīḍayante cakrākhye narake tathā .. 103 ..
4.6.d:
तिलपिंडैरिवाक्रम्य घोरैः कर्मभिरात्मनः ॥
तिलवत्सम्प्रपीडयन्ते चक्राख्ये नरके तथा ॥ 103 ॥
4.6.m: Overcome by their own terrible deeds, as if by sesame balls, / they are thoroughly crushed like sesame seeds in the hell named Cakra.

4.6.s:
bhidyaṃte cāpi talpeṣu lohabhrāṣṭreṣvanekadhā ..
tailapūrṇakaṭāheṣu sutapteṣu punaḥpunaḥ .. 104 ..
4.6.d:
भिद्यंते चापि तल्पेषु लोहभ्राष्ट्रेष्वनेकधा ॥
तैलपूर्णकटाहेषु सुतप्तेषु पुनःपुनः ॥ 104 ॥
4.6.m: And on couches of iron frying-pans they are shattered in many ways, / and again and again in intensely heated cauldrons filled with oil.

4.6.s:
bahuśaḥ pīḍyate jihvā yā'satyapriyavādinī ..
saṃdaṃśena sutaptena prapīḍyante ca pādayoḥ .. 1-5..
4.6.d:
बहुशः पीड्यते जिह्वा याऽसत्यप्रियवादिनी ॥
संदंशेन सुतप्तेन प्रपीड्यन्ते च पादयोः ॥ 1-5॥
4.6.m: Frequently crushed is the tongue that spoke untruth and flattery, / and they are squeezed at the feet with a red-hot pair of tongs.

4.6.s:
mithyāgamapravaktuśca dvijihvasya ca nirgatā ..
jihvārddhakrośavistīrṇā halaistīkṣṇaiśca bādhyate .. .. 106 ..
4.6.d:
मिथ्यागमप्रवक्तुश्च द्विजिह्वस्य च निर्गता ॥
जिह्वार्द्धक्रोशविस्तीर्णा हलैस्तीक्ष्णैश्च बाध्यते ॥ ॥ 106 ॥
4.6.m: And the tongue of the false teacher of tradition, of the two-tongued [liar], protruding / half a krośa in width, is afflicted with sharp ploughs.

4.6.s:
nirbhartsayaṃti ye krūrā mātaraṃ pitaraṃ gurum ..
teṣāṃ vakṣa ulūkābhirmukhamāpūrya sevyate ..107..
4.6.d:
निर्भर्त्सयंति ये क्रूरा मातरं पितरं गुरुम् ॥
तेषां वक्ष उलूकाभिर्मुखमापूर्य सेव्यते ॥107॥
4.6.m: As for those cruel ones who reviled mother, father, or guru, / their chest is subjected [to torment], their mouth having been filled with embers.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena tāmreṇa tu punaḥpunaḥ ..
hatenāpūryate'tyarthaṃ taptatailaiśca tanmukham .. 108 ..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन ताम्रेण तु पुनःपुनः ॥
हतेनापूर्यतेऽत्यर्थं तप्ततैलैश्च तन्मुखम् ॥ 108 ॥
4.6.m: Then, with blazing caustic, and again and again with molten copper, / and with boiling oils, that mouth, struck violently, is filled.

4.6.s:
itastataḥ punarvaktraṃ bhṛśamāpūrya hanyate ..
viṣṭhābhiḥ kṛmibhiścāpi suvarṇaharaṇairnaraḥ .. 109 ..
4.6.d:
इतस्ततः पुनर्वक्त्रं भृशमापूर्य हन्यते ॥
विष्ठाभिः कृमिभिश्चापि सुवर्णहरणैर्नरः ॥ 109 ॥
4.6.m: Having filled his mouth abundantly on this side and that, a man / who stole gold is beaten again with excrement and with worms.

4.6.s:
pariṣvajati cātyugrāṃ pradīptāṃ lohaśālmalīm ..
hanyate pṛṣṭhadeśe ca punastīkṣṇairmahāghanaiḥ .. 4.6.110 ..
4.6.d:
परिष्वजति चात्युग्रां प्रदीप्तां लोहशाल्मलीम् ॥
हन्यते पृष्ठदेशे च पुनस्तीक्ष्णैर्महाघनैः ॥ 4.6.110 ॥
4.6.m: And he embraces a most terrifying, blazing iron silk-cotton tree, / and on his back he is struck again with sharp, heavy clubs.

4.6.s:
daṃtureṇātikūṭena krakacena balīyasā ..
śiraḥ prabhṛti pādāṃtaṃ ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmajaiḥ ..
khādyate svāni māṃsāni pāyate śoṇitaṃ svakam .. 111 ..
4.6.d:
दंतुरेणातिकूटेन क्रकचेन बलीयसा ॥
शिरः प्रभृति पादांतं घोरैः कर्मभिरात्मजैः ॥
खाद्यते स्वानि मांसानि पायते शोणितं स्वकम् ॥ 111 ॥
4.6.m: By a jagged, exceedingly treacherous, powerful saw, / from head to foot, because of the terrible deeds born of oneself, / he is made to eat his own flesh and made to drink his own blood.

4.6.s:
annaṃ pānaṃ na dattaṃ yairmūḍhairnāpyanumoditam..
ikṣuvatte prapīḍyante jarjarīkṛtamastakāḥ .. 112 ..
4.6.d:
अन्नं पानं न दत्तं यैर्मूढैर्नाप्यनुमोदितम्॥
इक्षुवत्ते प्रपीड्यन्ते जर्जरीकृतमस्तकाः ॥ 112 ॥
4.6.m: Those fools by whom food and drink were not given, nor even approved of, / are pressed like sugarcane, their heads completely shattered.

4.6.s:
asitālavane ghore cchidyaṃte khaṃḍakhaṃḍaśaḥ..
sūcībhirbhinnasarvāṃgāstaptaśūlapraropitāḥ ..
saṃbādhyamānā vivaśāḥ kliśyaṃte na mriyaṃti vai .. 113 ..
4.6.d:
असितालवने घोरे च्छिद्यंते खंडखंडशः॥
सूचीभिर्भिन्नसर्वांगास्तप्तशूलप्ररोपिताः ॥
संबाध्यमाना विवशाः क्लिश्यंते न म्रियंति वै ॥ 113 ॥
4.6.m: In the dreadful forest of sword-leaves, they are hacked into pieces; / with all their limbs pierced by needles, mounted upon red-hot stakes, / being harassed, helpless, they suffer and indeed do not die.

4.6.s:
dehādutsādyamāṃsāni bhidyaṃte'sthīni mudgaraiḥ ..
dṛṣṭirākṛṣyate tūrṇaṃ yamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ .. 114 ..
4.6.d:
देहादुत्साद्यमांसानि भिद्यंतेऽस्थीनि मुद्गरैः ॥
दृष्टिराकृष्यते तूर्णं यमदूतैर्बलोत्कटैः ॥ 114 ॥
4.6.m: Tearing the flesh from the body, their bones are broken with mallets; / their eyesight is swiftly plucked out by Yama's mighty messengers.

4.6.s:
nirastāste nirucchvāsāstiṣṭhaṃti narake dhruvam ..
ucchvasaṃti sadā śvāsairvālukāvadanāvṛtāḥ .. 115 ..
4.6.d:
निरस्तास्ते निरुच्छ्वासास्तिष्ठंति नरके ध्रुवम् ॥
उच्छ्वसंति सदा श्वासैर्वालुकावदनावृताः ॥ 115 ॥
4.6.m: Cast out and breathless, they remain in hell constantly; / their mouths covered with sand, they continually gasp for breath.

4.6.s:
raurave rodamānāśca pīḍyante vividhaiḥ śaraiḥ ..
mahārauravapīḍābhirmahatībhistadaṃtike .. 116 ..
4.6.d:
रौरवे रोदमानाश्च पीड्यन्ते विविधैः शरैः ॥
महारौरवपीडाभिर्महतीभिस्तदंतिके ॥ 116 ॥
4.6.m: Weeping in Raurava, they are afflicted with various arrows, / and near it with the immense torments of Mahāraurava.

4.6.s:
padorāsye gude caiva pārśve corasi mastake ..
nikhanyaṃte ghanaistīkṣṇaiḥ sutaptairlohaśaṃkubhiḥ .. 117 ..
4.6.d:
पदोरास्ये गुदे चैव पार्श्वे चोरसि मस्तके ॥
निखन्यंते घनैस्तीक्ष्णैः सुतप्तैर्लोहशंकुभिः ॥ 117 ॥
4.6.m: Into the two feet, the mouth, the anus, the sides, the chest, and the head, / solid, sharp, intensely heated iron stakes are driven.

4.6.s:
sutaptavālukāyāṃ ca praluṭhyante punaḥpunaḥ ..
jatupaṃke bhṛśaṃ tapte kṣiprā krandaṃti vistaram .. 118 ..
4.6.d:
सुतप्तवालुकायां च प्रलुठ्यन्ते पुनःपुनः ॥
जतुपंके भृशं तप्ते क्षिप्रा क्रन्दंति विस्तरम् ॥ 118 ॥
4.6.m: And they are rolled again and again in intensely heated sand; / cast into intensely hot mire of lac, they wail loudly.

4.6.s:
tenatenaiva rūpeṇa hasante pāradārikam ..
gāḍhamāliṅgyate nārīṃ jvalaṃtīṃ lohanirmitām .. 119 ..
4.6.d:
तेनतेनैव रूपेण हसन्ते पारदारिकम् ॥
गाढमालिङ्ग्यते नारीं ज्वलंतीं लोहनिर्मिताम् ॥ 119 ॥
4.6.m: Laughing at the adulterer in that very form, / he is made to embrace tightly a blazing woman made of iron.

4.6.s:
pūrvākāraṃ ca puruṣaṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ samaṃtataḥ ..
duścāriṇīḥ striyo gāḍhamāliṃgaṃti vadaṃti ca .. 4.6.120 ..
4.6.d:
पूर्वाकारं च पुरुषं प्रज्वलंतं समंततः ॥
दुश्चारिणीः स्त्रियो गाढमालिंगंति वदंति च ॥ 4.6.120 ॥
4.6.m: And women of wicked conduct tightly embrace a man of their previous form, / blazing all around, and [the messengers] say:

4.6.s:
kiṃ pradhāvasi vegena te na mokṣo'sti sāṃpratam ..
laṃghitaste yathā bhartā pāpaṃ bhuṃkṣva tathādhunā .. 121 ..
4.6.d:
किं प्रधावसि वेगेन ते न मोक्षोऽस्ति सांप्रतम् ॥
लंघितस्ते यथा भर्ता पापं भुंक्ष्व तथाधुना ॥ 121 ॥
4.6.m: "Why do you run with speed? There is no release for you now; / just as your husband was transgressed by you, so now enjoy your sin."

4.6.s:
lohakumbhe tathā kṣiptāḥ savidhānaiḥ śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
mṛdvagninātha pacyaṃte svapāpaireva mānavāḥ .. 122 ..
4.6.d:
लोहकुम्भे तथा क्षिप्ताः सविधानैः शनैःशनैः ॥
मृद्वग्निनाथ पच्यंते स्वपापैरेव मानवाः ॥ 122 ॥
4.6.m: Likewise cast into an iron jar, slowly, by prescribed means / men are cooked with a gentle fire solely by their own sins.

4.6.s:
kvaṇaṃtyudūkhale sāsrāḥ prakṣipyaṃte śilāsu ca ..
kṣipyaṃte cāṃdhakūpeṣu daśyaṃte bhramarairbhṛśam .. 123 ..
4.6.d:
क्वणंत्युदूखले सास्राः प्रक्षिप्यंते शिलासु च ॥
क्षिप्यंते चांधकूपेषु दश्यंते भ्रमरैर्भृशम् ॥ 123 ॥
4.6.m: Weeping with tears in a mortar, they groan and are cast upon rocks; / and they are cast into blind wells and bitten severely by bees.

4.6.s:
kṛmibhirbhinnasarvāṃgāḥ śataśo jarjarīkṛtāḥ ..
sutīkṣṇakṣārakūpepu kṣipyaṃte tadanaṃtaram.. 124 ..
4.6.d:
कृमिभिर्भिन्नसर्वांगाः शतशो जर्जरीकृताः ॥
सुतीक्ष्णक्षारकूपेपु क्षिप्यंते तदनंतरम्॥ 124 ॥
4.6.m: Their bodies completely pierced by worms and shattered into hundreds [of pieces], / they are immediately cast into pits of extremely sharp caustic.

4.6.s:
mahājvāle ca narake pāpāḥ phūtkārayaṃti ca ..
itastataśca dhāvaṃti dahyamānāstadarcciṣā .. 125 ..
4.6.d:
महाज्वाले च नरके पापाः फूत्कारयंति च ॥
इतस्ततश्च धावंति दह्यमानास्तदर्च्चिषा ॥ 125 ॥
4.6.m: And in the Mahājvāla hell, the sinners scream / and run hither and thither, burning from its flames.

4.6.s:
pṛṣṭhe cānīya jaṃghe dve vinyaste skandhayoḥ sthite ..
tayormadhyena cākṛṣya bāhupṛṣṭhena gāḍhataḥ ..
baddhvā parasparaṃ sarvaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ gāḍharajjubhi. .. 126 ..
4.6.d:
पृष्ठे चानीय जंघे द्वे विन्यस्ते स्कन्धयोः स्थिते ॥
तयोर्मध्येन चाकृष्य बाहुपृष्ठेन गाढतः ॥
बद्ध्वा परस्परं सर्वं सुदृढं गाढरज्जुभि॥। 126 ॥
4.6.m: Bringing both shanks behind the back and placing them on the shoulders, / pulling [the arms] through the middle of the two, behind the back, tightly, / binding everything firmly together with strong ropes,

4.6.s:
pīḍayaṃti susaṃrabdhā bhramarāstīkṣṇalohajāḥ ..
mānināṃ krodhināṃ caiva purā pāpasya saṃśayāt .. 127 ..
4.6.d:
पीडयंति सुसंरब्धा भ्रमरास्तीक्ष्णलोहजाः ॥
मानिनां क्रोधिनां चैव पुरा पापस्य संशयात् ॥ 127 ॥
4.6.m: furious hornets born of sharp iron torment [them], / [the punishment] for the proud and the angry, on account of their former sin.

4.6.s:
pāpānāṃ narake puṃsāṃ ghṛṣyate caṃdanaṃ yathā ..
śarīrābhyaṃtaragataṃ taruṇānāṃ ca dāruṇam .. 128 ..
4.6.d:
पापानां नरके पुंसां घृष्यते चंदनं यथा ॥
शरीराभ्यंतरगतं तरुणानां च दारुणम् ॥ 128 ॥
4.6.m: In hell, [the bodies] of sinful men are rubbed down just as sandalwood [is rubbed]— / a dreadful [torment] penetrating into the interior of the bodies even of the young.

4.6.s:
piṃḍabaṃdho smṛto yāmyo mahājvāleṣu yātanāḥ ..
rajjubhirveṣṭitāṃgāśca praliptāḥ kardamena ca ..
karīṣarūkṣavahnau ca pacyaṃte na mriyaṃti ca .. 129 ..
4.6.d:
पिंडबंधो स्मृतो याम्यो महाज्वालेषु यातनाः ॥
रज्जुभिर्वेष्टितांगाश्च प्रलिप्ताः कर्दमेन च ॥
करीषरूक्षवह्नौ च पच्यंते न म्रियंति च ॥ 129 ॥
4.6.m: This is known as the Yama-binding of the body; the torments in Mahājvāla [are as follows]: / with their limbs wrapped in ropes and smeared with mud, / they are cooked in dry fire fueled by cow dung, yet they do not die.

4.6.s:
sutīkṣṇakṣāratoyena śarkarāsu śilāsu ca ..
ā pāpasaṃkṣayātpāpā ghṛṣyaṃte caṃdanaṃ yathā .. 4.6.130 ..
4.6.d:
सुतीक्ष्णक्षारतोयेन शर्करासु शिलासु च ॥
आ पापसंक्षयात्पापा घृष्यंते चंदनं यथा ॥ 4.6.130 ॥
4.6.m: With extremely pungent alkaline water, upon gravel and rocks, / sinners are rubbed down like sandalwood until their sin is destroyed.

4.6.s:
śarīrābhyantaragataiḥ prabhūtaiḥ kṛmibhirnarāḥ ..
bhakṣyaṃte tīkṣṇavadanairādehaprakṣayāṭ bhṛśam .. 131 ..
4.6.d:
शरीराभ्यन्तरगतैः प्रभूतैः कृमिभिर्नराः ॥
भक्ष्यंते तीक्ष्णवदनैरादेहप्रक्षयाट् भृशम् ॥ 131 ॥
4.6.m: By abundant worms with sharp mouths that enter inside their bodies, / men are devoured violently until their bodies perish.

4.6.s:
kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye kṣiptāḥ pūtimāṃsasya rāśiṣu ..
tiṣṭhantyudvignahṛdayāḥ parvatābhyāṃ ca pīḍitāḥ .. 132 ..
4.6.d:
कृमीणां निचये क्षिप्ताः पूतिमांसस्य राशिषु ॥
तिष्ठन्त्युद्विग्नहृदयाः पर्वताभ्यां च पीडिताः ॥ 132 ॥
4.6.m: Cast into an accumulation of worms and onto heaps of rotting flesh, / they remain with agitated hearts, crushed between two mountains.

4.6.s:
sutaptavajralepena śarīramanulipyate ..
adhomukhordhvapādāśca dhṛtāstapyaṃti vahniṣu .. 133 ..
4.6.d:
सुतप्तवज्रलेपेन शरीरमनुलिप्यते ॥
अधोमुखोर्ध्वपादाश्च धृतास्तप्यंति वह्निषु ॥ 133 ॥
4.6.m: Their bodies are smeared with a paste of boiling diamond-pitch; / held upside-down with feet upwards, they burn in fires.

4.6.s:
vadanāṃte pravinyastaṃ sutaptāyomayaṃ guḍam ..
te khādaṃti parādhīnā hanyamānāstu mudgaraiḥ .. 134 ..
4.6.d:
वदनांते प्रविन्यस्तं सुतप्तायोमयं गुडम् ॥
ते खादंति पराधीना हन्यमानास्तु मुद्गरैः ॥ 134 ॥
4.6.m: A glowing iron ball is placed inside their mouths; / helpless, struck with clubs, they are made to chew it.

4.6.s:
ye śivāyatanārāmavāpīkūpamaṭhāṃga ṇāt ..
abhidravaṃti pāpiṣṭhā narāstatra vasaṃti ca .. 135 ..
4.6.d:
ये शिवायतनारामवापीकूपमठांग णात् ॥
अभिद्रवंति पापिष्ठा नरास्तत्र वसंति च ॥ 135 ॥
4.6.m: Those most sinful men who run away from / the compound of a temple of Śiva, a grove, a pool, a well, or a monastery, and live there,

4.6.s:
vyāyāmodvartanābhyaṃgasnānamāpānabhojanam ..
krīḍanaṃ maithunaṃ dyūtamāca raṃti ramaṃti ca .. 136 ..
4.6.d:
व्यायामोद्वर्तनाभ्यंगस्नानमापानभोजनम् ॥
क्रीडनं मैथुनं द्यूतमाच रंति रमंति च ॥ 136 ॥
4.6.m: who practice and delight in physical exercise, body-scrubbing, oil-massage, / bathing, drinking-parties, dining, sports, sexual intercourse, and gambling—

4.6.s:
te bādhairvividhairghorairikṣuyantrādipīḍanaiḥ ..
nirayāgniṣu pacyaṃte yāvadācandratārakam .. 137 ..
4.6.d:
ते बाधैर्विविधैर्घोरैरिक्षुयन्त्रादिपीडनैः ॥
निरयाग्निषु पच्यंते यावदाचन्द्रतारकम् ॥ 137 ॥
4.6.m: they are cooked in the fires of hell as long as the moon and stars endure, / through various dreadful torments, being crushed in sugarcane-presses and the like.

4.6.s:
ye śṛṇvaṃti gurorniṃdāṃ teṣāṃ karṇaḥ prapūryyate ..
agnivarṇairayaḥkīlaistaptatāmrādibhirdrutaiḥ .. 138 ..
4.6.d:
ये शृण्वंति गुरोर्निंदां तेषां कर्णः प्रपूर्य्यते ॥
अग्निवर्णैरयःकीलैस्तप्तताम्रादिभिर्द्रुतैः ॥ 138 ॥
4.6.m: For those who listen to slander of the guru, their ear is filled / with fire-colored iron spikes, molten copper, and other [metals],

4.6.s:
trapusīsārakūṭādyaiḥ kṣāreṇa jatunā punaḥ ..
kramādāpūryate karṇo narakeṣu ca yātanāḥ ..
anukrameṇa sarveṣu bhavaṃtyetāḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 139 ..
4.6.d:
त्रपुसीसारकूटाद्यैः क्षारेण जतुना पुनः ॥
क्रमादापूर्यते कर्णो नरकेषु च यातनाः ॥
अनुक्रमेण सर्वेषु भवंत्येताः समंततः ॥ 139 ॥
4.6.m: with tin, lead, brass, and the like, and again with alkali and lac; / gradually their ear is filled, and such torments / occur everywhere in all the hells in turn.

4.6.s:
sarveṃdriyāṇāmapyevaṃ kramātpāpena yātanāḥ ..
bhavaṃti ghorāḥ pratyekaṃ śarīre tatkṛtena ca .. 4.6.140 ..
4.6.d:
सर्वेंद्रियाणामप्येवं क्रमात्पापेन यातनाः ॥
भवंति घोराः प्रत्येकं शरीरे तत्कृतेन च ॥ 4.6.140 ॥
4.6.m: In this way, terrible torments occur for all the senses in turn, / each according to the sin committed by the body.

4.6.s:
sparśalobhena ye mūḍhāḥ saṃspṛśaṃti parastriyam ..
teṣāṃ tvagagnivarṇābhiḥ sūcībhiḥ pūryate bhṛśam ..141..
4.6.d:
स्पर्शलोभेन ये मूढाः संस्पृशंति परस्त्रियम् ॥
तेषां त्वगग्निवर्णाभिः सूचीभिः पूर्यते भृशम् ॥141॥
4.6.m: Those fools who, through longing for touch, touch another's wife, / their skin is pierced profusely with needles having the color of fire.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣārādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ śarīramanulipyate ..
yātanā ca mahākaṣṭā sarveṣu narakeṣu ca .. 142 ..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारादिभिः सर्वैः शरीरमनुलिप्यते ॥
यातना च महाकष्टा सर्वेषु नरकेषु च ॥ 142 ॥
4.6.m: Then the body is smeared with all [substances such as] alkali; / and there is extremely painful torment in all the hells.

4.6.s:
guroḥ kurvaṃti bhrukuṭiṃ krūraṃ cakṣuśca ye narāḥ ..
paradārāṃśca paśyaṃti lubdhāḥ snigdhena cakṣuṣā ..143..
4.6.d:
गुरोः कुर्वंति भ्रुकुटिं क्रूरं चक्षुश्च ये नराः ॥
परदारांश्च पश्यंति लुब्धाः स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा ॥143॥
4.6.m: Those men who knit their brows at the guru and cast cruel eyes [at him], / and who look lustfully at another's wife with an affectionate gaze,

4.6.s:
sūcībhiragnivarṇābhisteṣāṃ netraṃ prapūryate ..
kṣārādyaiśca kramātsarvairdehe sarvāśca yātanāḥ .. 144 ...
4.6.d:
सूचीभिरग्निवर्णाभिस्तेषां नेत्रं प्रपूर्यते ॥
क्षाराद्यैश्च क्रमात्सर्वैर्देहे सर्वाश्च यातनाः ॥ 144 ॥।
4.6.m: their eyes are filled with needles having the color of fire, / and their bodies [endure] all torments in turn with alkali and other [substances].

4.6.s:
devāgniguruviprāṇāṃ ye'nivedya prabhuṃjate ..
lohakīlaśataistaptaistajjihvāsyaṃ prapūryate .. 145 ..
4.6.d:
देवाग्निगुरुविप्राणां येऽनिवेद्य प्रभुंजते ॥
लोहकीलशतैस्तप्तैस्तज्जिह्वास्यं प्रपूर्यते ॥ 145 ॥
4.6.m: Those who eat without first offering to the gods, the fire, the guru, and the brāhmaṇas, / their mouth and tongue are filled with hundreds of heated iron spikes.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena tailatāmrādibhiḥ kramāt ...
śarīre ca mahāghorāścitrā narakayātanāḥ ..146..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन तैलताम्रादिभिः क्रमात् ॥।
शरीरे च महाघोराश्चित्रा नरकयातनाः ॥146॥
4.6.m: Then, in turn, with blazing alkali, oil, copper, and the like, / most terrible and diverse hell-torments [are inflicted] on the body.

4.6.s:
ye śivārāmapuṣpāṇi lobhātsaṃgṛhya pāṇinā ..
jighraṃti mūḍhamanasaḥ śirasā dhārayaṃti ca ..147...
4.6.d:
ये शिवारामपुष्पाणि लोभात्संगृह्य पाणिना ॥
जिघ्रंति मूढमनसः शिरसा धारयंति च ॥147॥।
4.6.m: Those foolish-minded who, grasping with the hand out of greed, / smell flowers from Śiva's grove and wear them on their heads,

4.6.s:
āpūryate śirasteṣāṃ sutaptairlohaśaṃkubhiḥ ..
nāsikā cātibahuśastataḥ kṣārādibhiḥ punaḥ .. 148 ..
4.6.d:
आपूर्यते शिरस्तेषां सुतप्तैर्लोहशंकुभिः ॥
नासिका चातिबहुशस्ततः क्षारादिभिः पुनः ॥ 148 ॥
4.6.m: their head is filled with glowing iron pegs, / as is the nose repeatedly, and then again with alkali and other [substances].

4.6.s:
ye niṃdaṃti mahātmānamācāryaṃ dharmadeśikam ..
śivabhaktāṃśca ye mūḍhāḥ śivadharmaṃ ca śāśvatam .. 149 ..
4.6.d:
ये निंदंति महात्मानमाचार्यं धर्मदेशिकम् ॥
शिवभक्तांश्च ये मूढाः शिवधर्मं च शाश्वतम् ॥ 149 ॥
4.6.m: Those fools who revile the high-souled master who teaches the dharma, / the devotees of Śiva, and the eternal Śaiva dharma,

4.6.s:
teṣāmurasi kaṃṭhe ca jihvāyāṃ daṃtasaṃdhiṣu ..
tālukoṣṭhe ca nāsāyāṃ mūrdhni sarvāṃgasaṃ dhiṣu .. 4.6.150 ..
4.6.d:
तेषामुरसि कंठे च जिह्वायां दंतसंधिषु ॥
तालुकोष्ठे च नासायां मूर्ध्नि सर्वांगसं धिषु ॥ 4.6.150 ॥
4.6.m: in their chest, throat, tongue, joints of the teeth, / palate, abdomen, nose, head, and all the joints of their limbs,

4.6.s:
agnivarṇāḥ sutaptāśca triśikhā lohaśaṃkavaḥ ..
ākhanyaṃte subahuśaḥ sthāneṣveteṣu mudgaraiḥ .. 151 ..
4.6.d:
अग्निवर्णाः सुतप्ताश्च त्रिशिखा लोहशंकवः ॥
आखन्यंते सुबहुशः स्थानेष्वेतेषु मुद्गरैः ॥ 151 ॥
4.6.m: heated three-pronged iron stakes, having the color of fire, / are hammered repeatedly into these places with clubs.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa taptena tāmreṇa trapuṇā punaḥ ..
taptatailādibhiḥ sarvairāpūryaṃte samaṃtataḥ .. 152 ..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारेण तप्तेन ताम्रेण त्रपुणा पुनः ॥
तप्ततैलादिभिः सर्वैरापूर्यंते समंततः ॥ 152 ॥
4.6.m: Then with alkali, molten copper, tin, / and heated oil and other [liquids], they are filled on all sides.

4.6.s:
kṣāratāmrādibhirdīptairdahyaṃte bahuśaḥ punaḥ ..
narakeṣu ca sarveṣu vicitrā dehayā tanāḥ .. 153 ..
4.6.d:
क्षारताम्रादिभिर्दीप्तैर्दह्यंते बहुशः पुनः ॥
नरकेषु च सर्वेषु विचित्रा देहया तनाः ॥ 153 ॥
4.6.m: Burned repeatedly with blazing alkali, copper, and the like, / various bodily torments [are inflicted] in all the hells.

4.6.s:
bhavaṃti bahuśaḥ kaṣṭāḥ pāṇipādasamudbhavāḥ ..
śivāyatanaparyaṃte śivārāme ca kutracit .. 154 ..
4.6.d:
भवंति बहुशः कष्टाः पाणिपादसमुद्भवाः ॥
शिवायतनपर्यंते शिवारामे च कुत्रचित् ॥ 154 ॥
4.6.m: Frequent and painful [torments] arise from [sins committed with] hands and feet. / Those sinners who, around the precincts of a temple of Śiva or anywhere in a grove of Śiva,

4.6.s:
samutsṛjaṃti ye pāpāḥ purīṣaṃ mūtrameva vā ..
teṣāṃ liṃgaṃ savṛṣaṇaṃ cūrṇyate lohamudgaraiḥ .. 155 ..
4.6.d:
समुत्सृजंति ये पापाः पुरीषं मूत्रमेव वा ॥
तेषां लिंगं सवृषणं चूर्ण्यते लोहमुद्गरैः ॥ 155 ॥
4.6.m: discharge feces or urine, / their penis along with the testicles is crushed with iron clubs.

4.6.s:
sūcībhiragnivarṇābhistataścāpūryate punaḥ ..
lohadaṇḍaśca sumahānagnivarṇaḥ sakaṃṭakaḥ ..
ākhanyate gude teṣāṃ yāvanmūrdhni vinirgataḥ ..156..
4.6.d:
सूचीभिरग्निवर्णाभिस्ततश्चापूर्यते पुनः ॥
लोहदण्डश्च सुमहानग्निवर्णः सकंटकः ॥
आखन्यते गुदे तेषां यावन्मूर्ध्नि विनिर्गतः ॥156॥
4.6.m: Then it is filled again with needles having the color of fire; / and a huge iron rod, having the color of fire and bearing thorns, / is driven into their anus until it comes out at the crown of the head.

4.6.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa mahatā tāmreṇa trapuṇā punaḥ ..
drutenāpūryate gāḍhaṃ gudaṃ śiśnaṃ hi dehinām..157..
4.6.d:
ततः क्षारेण महता ताम्रेण त्रपुणा पुनः ॥
द्रुतेनापूर्यते गाढं गुदं शिश्नं हि देहिनाम्॥157॥
4.6.m: Then, with strong alkali, copper, and tin, / in molten form, the anus and penis of the embodied souls are filled tightly.

4.6.s:
manaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ ca yasmāduktaṃ pravarttakam ..
tasmādindriyaduḥkhena jāyate tatsuduḥkhitam ..158..
4.6.d:
मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणां च यस्मादुक्तं प्रवर्त्तकम् ॥
तस्मादिन्द्रियदुःखेन जायते तत्सुदुःखितम् ॥158॥
4.6.m: Since the mind is said to be the instigator of all the senses, / it becomes exceedingly distressed through the suffering of the senses.

4.6.s:
dhane satyapi ye dānaṃ na prayacchaṃti tṛṣṇayā ...
atithiṃ cāvamanyaṃte kālaprāptaṃ gṛhāśrame ..159..
4.6.d:
धने सत्यपि ये दानं न प्रयच्छंति तृष्णया ॥।
अतिथिं चावमन्यंते कालप्राप्तं गृहाश्रमे ॥159॥
4.6.m: Those who, although having wealth, out of greed do not grant gifts, / and despise a guest who has arrived at the proper time in the householder's stage of life,

4.6.s:
te lohatoraṇe baddhā hastapādāvatāḍitāḥ ..
vidāritāṃgāḥ śuṣyaṃte tiṣṭhaṃtyabdaśataṃ narāḥ ..4.6.160..
4.6.d:
ते लोहतोरणे बद्धा हस्तपादावताडिताः ॥
विदारितांगाः शुष्यंते तिष्ठंत्यब्दशतं नराः ॥4.6.160॥
4.6.m: bound to an iron arch, beaten on hands and feet, / their limbs torn open, they dry up and remain for a hundred years.

4.6.s:
hastapādalalāṭeṣu kīlitā lohaśaṃkubhiḥ ..
nityaṃ ca nīvṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kīlakadvayanāḍitam .. 161 ..
4.6.d:
हस्तपादललाटेषु कीलिता लोहशंकुभिः ॥
नित्यं च नीवृतं वक्त्रं कीलकद्वयनाडितम् ॥ 161 ॥
4.6.m: Nailed through their hands, feet, and foreheads with iron pegs, / their mouth is constantly uncovered, pierced by two pegs.

4.6.s:
kṛmibhiḥ prāṇibhiścograirlohadaṃḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ ..
upadravairbahuvidhaiḥ sarpairmukharakaistataḥ .. 162 ..
4.6.d:
कृमिभिः प्राणिभिश्चोग्रैर्लोहदंडैश्च वायसैः ॥
उपद्रवैर्बहुविधैः सर्पैर्मुखरकैस्ततः ॥ 162 ॥
4.6.m: By worms, fierce creatures, iron rods, and crows, / by many kinds of afflictions, and then by noisy serpents,

4.6.s:
āpīḍyaṃte jihvāmūle nibadhya śṛṃkhalāḥ punaḥ ..
tiṣṭhaṃti laṃbamānāśca lohabhāraprapīḍitāḥ ..163..
4.6.d:
आपीड्यंते जिह्वामूले निबध्य शृंखलाः पुनः ॥
तिष्ठंति लंबमानाश्च लोहभारप्रपीडिताः ॥163॥
4.6.m: they are tormented; having fastened chains at the base of their tongue, / they remain hanging, oppressed by a heavy load of iron.

4.6.s:
snigdhe ca vṛṣaṇe naddhe lohabhāradvayaṃ punaḥ ..
tiṣṭhate laṃbamānaṃ ca bahubhāracaturguṇam .. 164 ..
4.6.d:
स्निग्धे च वृषणे नद्धे लोहभारद्वयं पुनः ॥
तिष्ठते लंबमानं च बहुभारचतुर्गुणम् ॥ 164 ॥
4.6.m: And fastened to the moist scrotum, two iron weights / remain hanging, four times heavier.

4.6.s:
tataḥ svamāṃsamutkṛtya tilamātrapramāṇataḥ ..
bhojanaṃ dīyate teṣāṃ sūcyagreṇa saśoṇitam .. 165 ..
4.6.d:
ततः स्वमांसमुत्कृत्य तिलमात्रप्रमाणतः ॥
भोजनं दीयते तेषां सूच्यग्रेण सशोणितम् ॥ 165 ॥
4.6.m: Then, carving off their own flesh in portions the size of a sesame seed, / it is given to them as food on the point of a needle, mixed with blood.

4.6.s:
yadā nirmāṃsatāṃ prāptāḥ kālena mahatā punaḥ ..
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena vapusteṣāṃ pralipyate .. 166 ..
4.6.d:
यदा निर्मांसतां प्राप्ताः कालेन महता पुनः ॥
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन वपुस्तेषां प्रलिप्यते ॥ 166 ॥
4.6.m: When, after a long time, they have become destitute of flesh, / their body is then smeared with blazing alkali.

4.6.s:
sicyaṃte varṣadhārābhiḥ śoṣyaṃte vāyunā punaḥ ..
sicyaṃte taptatailena prataptena samaṃtataḥ .. 167 ..
4.6.d:
सिच्यंते वर्षधाराभिः शोष्यंते वायुना पुनः ॥
सिच्यंते तप्ततैलेन प्रतप्तेन समंततः ॥ 167 ॥
4.6.m: They are sprinkled with torrents of rain, and then dried up by the wind; / they are sprinkled all over with boiling, burning oil.

4.6.s:
paścātte vahninā bhūyo dūrasthena śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ..
niḥśeṣayātanābhiśca pīḍyaṃte kramaśaḥ punaḥ .. 168 ..
4.6.d:
पश्चात्ते वह्निना भूयो दूरस्थेन शनैः शनैः ॥
निःशेषयातनाभिश्च पीड्यंते क्रमशः पुनः ॥ 168 ॥
4.6.m: Afterwards, they are tortured gradually again by fire / situated at a distance, slowly, slowly, and with every kind of torment.

4.6.s:
bhṛśaṃ bubhukṣayā pīḍā mūrcchayātipipāsayā ..
atyuṣṇenātiśītena pāpānāṃ samareṇa ca .. 169 ..
4.6.d:
भृशं बुभुक्षया पीडा मूर्च्छयातिपिपासया ॥
अत्युष्णेनातिशीतेन पापानां समरेण च ॥ 169 ॥
4.6.m: Violent pain comes upon the sinners from hunger, from fainting, from extreme thirst, / from intense heat, from intense cold, and from conflict.

4.6.s:
evamādimahāghorā yātanāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ ..
ekaike narake caiva śataśotha sahasraśaḥ .. 4.6.170 ..
4.6.d:
एवमादिमहाघोरा यातनाः पापकारिणः ॥
एकैके नरके चैव शतशोथ सहस्रशः ॥ 4.6.170 ॥
4.6.m: Such exceedingly terrible torments as these / afflict the evil-doers in each hell by the hundreds and thousands.

4.6.s:
pratyekaṃ yātanāścitrāḥ sarveṣu narakeṣu ca ..
kaṣṭaṃ varṣaśatenāpi soḍhuṃ sarvaiśca nārake ..171..
4.6.d:
प्रत्येकं यातनाश्चित्राः सर्वेषु नरकेषु च ॥
कष्टं वर्षशतेनापि सोढुं सर्वैश्च नारके ॥171॥
4.6.m: The torments are manifold and distinct in every hell; / hard indeed is it for all those in hell to endure them, even for a hundred years.

4.6.s:
ete ca vividhairghorairyātyamānāśca karmabhiḥ ..
mriyante naiva pāpiṣṭhā vividhāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ .. .. 172 ..
4.6.d:
एते च विविधैर्घोरैर्यात्यमानाश्च कर्मभिः ॥
म्रियन्ते नैव पापिष्ठा विविधाः पापकारिणः ॥ ॥ 172 ॥
4.6.m: Being tortured by these various terrible deeds, / the most wicked, the various wrongdoers, do not die at all.

4.6.s:
mahāghorābhighorākhyā kālāgnisadṛśopamāḥ ..
śrutairetairmahāraudrairmriyante mṛducetasaḥ .. 173 ..
4.6.d:
महाघोराभिघोराख्या कालाग्निसदृशोपमाः ॥
श्रुतैरेतैर्महारौद्रैर्म्रियन्ते मृदुचेतसः ॥ 173 ॥
4.6.m: [These hells,] called the Most Terrible and Exceedingly Terrifying, resemble the fire of time; / upon hearing of these exceedingly dreadful [terrors], the soft-hearted die.

4.6.s:
tatastenātra kathitāḥ pāpā gacchaṃti tānsvayam ..
putramitrakalatrārthaṃ yadā puṇyaṃ tvapākṛtam .. 174 ..
4.6.d:
ततस्तेनात्र कथिताः पापा गच्छंति तान्स्वयम् ॥
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रार्थं यदा पुण्यं त्वपाकृतम् ॥ 174 ॥
4.6.m: Then the sins spoken of here go of themselves to them: / 'When merit was cast aside for the sake of son, friend, or wife,

4.6.s:
ekākī dahyate tena na ca paśyati tāni saḥ ..
ātmanā ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ bhoktavyaṃ dhruvamātmanā .. 175 ..
4.6.d:
एकाकी दह्यते तेन न च पश्यति तानि सः ॥
आत्मना च कृतं पापं भोक्तव्यं ध्रुवमात्मना ॥ 175 ॥
4.6.m: one is burned alone on that account, and does not see them; / and the evil deed done by oneself must certainly be experienced by oneself.'

4.6.s:
tatkimanyopaghātārthaṃ mūḍha pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā ..
evaṃ dūtairupālabdhāste pṛcchaṃti tataḥ punaḥ .. 176 ..
4.6.d:
तत्किमन्योपघातार्थं मूढ पापं कृतं त्वया ॥
एवं दूतैरुपालब्धास्ते पृच्छंति ततः पुनः ॥ 176 ॥
4.6.m: 'Why then was evil done by you, fool, to injure others?' / Reproached thus by the messengers [of Yama], they then ask again:

4.6.s:
kiyaṃtaṃ kena pāpena kālamatrāyate naraḥ ..
devadravyavināśena gurudrohādikarmabhiḥ ..
pāpātsarveṣu pacyaṃte narakeṣvāmahākṣayāt .. 377 ..
4.6.d:
कियंतं केन पापेन कालमत्रायते नरः ॥
देवद्रव्यविनाशेन गुरुद्रोहादिकर्मभिः ॥
पापात्सर्वेषु पच्यंते नरकेष्वामहाक्षयात् ॥ 377 ॥
4.6.m: 'For how long a time, and by what sin, does a man arrive here?' / By destroying the property of the gods, by betraying one's guru, and other such deeds, / the wicked are cooked in all the hells until the great dissolution.

4.6.s:
mahāpātakinaścāpi sarveṣu narakeṣviha ..
ācaṃdratārakaṃ yāvatpīḍyaṃte vividhairvadhaiḥ .. 178 ..
4.6.d:
महापातकिनश्चापि सर्वेषु नरकेष्विह ॥
आचंद्रतारकं यावत्पीड्यंते विविधैर्वधैः ॥ 178 ॥
4.6.m: And the perpetrators of great sins in all the hells here / are tortured with various killings as long as the moon and the stars endure.

4.6.s:
mahāpātakinaścānye narakārṇavakoṭiṣu ..
caturdaśasu pacyaṃte kalārdhaṃ vividhairvadhaiḥ .. 179 ..
4.6.d:
महापातकिनश्चान्ये नरकार्णवकोटिषु ॥
चतुर्दशसु पच्यंते कलार्धं विविधैर्वधैः ॥ 179 ॥
4.6.m: Other perpetrators of great sins are cooked in the fourteen / crores of hell-oceans with various killings for half a kalpa.

4.6.s:
upapātakinaścāpi tadarthaṃ yāṃti mānavāḥ ..
śeṣapāpaistadardhaṃ tu kālaṃ cāpi tathāvidham .. 4.6.180 ..
4.6.d:
उपपातकिनश्चापि तदर्थं यांति मानवाः ॥
शेषपापैस्तदर्धं तु कालं चापि तथाविधम् ॥ 4.6.180 ॥
4.6.m: Perpetrators of secondary sins go for half that duration; / and for the remaining sins, [they go] for half of that, and for a corresponding time.

4.6.s:
tasmātpāpaṃ na kurvīta caṃcale jīvite sati ..
pāpena hi dhruvaṃ yāṃti narakeṣu narāḥ svayam .. 181 ..
4.6.d:
तस्मात्पापं न कुर्वीत चंचले जीविते सति ॥
पापेन हि ध्रुवं यांति नरकेषु नराः स्वयम् ॥ 181 ॥
4.6.m: Therefore, one should not commit sin while life is unsteady; / for by sin, men certainly go to the hells of themselves.

4.6.s:
yaḥ karoti naraḥ pāpaṃ tasyātmā dhruvamapriyaḥ ..
pāpasyeha phalaṃ duḥkhaṃ tadbhoktavyamihātmanā .. 182 ..
4.6.d:
यः करोति नरः पापं तस्यात्मा ध्रुवमप्रियः ॥
पापस्येह फलं दुःखं तद्भोक्तव्यमिहात्मना ॥ 182 ॥
4.6.m: The man who commits sin certainly holds his own self unloved; / the fruit of sin in this world is misery, and that must be experienced here by oneself.

4.6.s:
kathaṃ te pāpaniratā narā rātriṣu śerate ..
maraṇāṃtaritā yeṣāṃ nārakī tīvrayātanā .. 183 ..
4.6.d:
कथं ते पापनिरता नरा रात्रिषु शेरते ॥
मरणांतरिता येषां नारकी तीव्रयातना ॥ 183 ॥
4.6.m: How can those men devoted to sin sleep during the nights, / separated only by death from the sharp torment of hell?

4.6.s:
evaṃ kliṣṭaviśuddhāśca sāvaśeṣeṇa karmaṇā ..
tataḥ kṣitiṃ samāsādya jāyante dehinaḥ puna. ..
sthāvarā vividhākārāstṛṇagulmādibhedataḥ .. ... 184 ..
4.6.d:
एवं क्लिष्टविशुद्धाश्च सावशेषेण कर्मणा ॥
ततः क्षितिं समासाद्य जायन्ते देहिनः पुन॥।
स्थावरा विविधाकारास्तृणगुल्मादिभेदतः ॥ ॥। 184 ॥
4.6.m: Having been thus purified through affliction, with a remnant of their karma, / embodied souls then reach the earth and are born again / as immovable beings of various forms, distinguished as grasses, shrubs, and the like.

4.6.s:
tatrānubhūya duḥkhāni jāyaṃte kīṭayoniṣu ..
niṣkrāṃtāḥ kīṭayonibhyo jāyante pakṣiṇastataḥ .. 185 ..
4.6.d:
तत्रानुभूय दुःखानि जायंते कीटयोनिषु ॥
निष्क्रांताः कीटयोनिभ्यो जायन्ते पक्षिणस्ततः ॥ 185 ॥
4.6.m: Having experienced sufferings there, they are born in the wombs of worms and insects; / having emerged from the wombs of worms and insects, they are born as birds thereafter.

4.6.s:
saṃśliṣṭāḥ pakṣibhāvena bhavaṃti mṛgajādiṣu ..
mārgaṃ duḥkhamatikramya jāyaṃte paśuyoniṣu .. 186 ..
4.6.d:
संश्लिष्टाः पक्षिभावेन भवंति मृगजादिषु ॥
मार्गं दुःखमतिक्रम्य जायंते पशुयोनिषु ॥ 186 ॥
4.6.m: Held within the state of birds, they enter the species of deer and the like; / having crossed beyond that path of misery, they are born in the wombs of domestic animals.

4.6.s:
kramādgoyonimāsādya jāyante mānavāḥ punaḥ ..
evaṃ yoniṣu sarvāsu parikramya krameṇa tu ..
kālāṃtaravaśādyāṃti mānuṣyamatidurlabham .. 187 ..
4.6.d:
क्रमाद्गोयोनिमासाद्य जायन्ते मानवाः पुनः ॥
एवं योनिषु सर्वासु परिक्रम्य क्रमेण तु ॥
कालांतरवशाद्यांति मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम् ॥ 187 ॥
4.6.m: Reaching in due order the womb of cattle, they are born as human beings again; / having thus wandered through all wombs in succession, / they attain the exceedingly rare human state in the course of time.

4.6.s:
vyutkrameṇāpi mānuṣyaṃ prāpyate puṇyagocarāt ..
vicitrā gatayaḥ proktāḥ karmaṇāṃ gurulāghavāt .. 188 ..
4.6.d:
व्युत्क्रमेणापि मानुष्यं प्राप्यते पुण्यगोचरात् ॥
विचित्रा गतयः प्रोक्ताः कर्मणां गुरुलाघवात् ॥ 188 ॥
4.6.m: Human birth is also attained out of turn through the scope of merit; / the paths are declared to be manifold according to the weight or lightness of deeds.

4.6.s:
mānuṣyaṃ yaḥ samāsādya svargamokṣaprasādhakam ..
dvayorna sādhayatyekaṃ sa mṛtastapyate ciram .. .. 189 ..
4.6.d:
मानुष्यं यः समासाद्य स्वर्गमोक्षप्रसाधकम् ॥
द्वयोर्न साधयत्येकं स मृतस्तप्यते चिरम् ॥ ॥ 189 ॥
4.6.m: He who, having attained human birth, which accomplishes heaven and liberation, / does not achieve one of the two, burns with remorse for a long time when dead.

4.6.s:
devāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ mānuṣyamatidurlabham ..
tatsaṃprāpya kathāḥ kuryānna gacchennarakaṃ yathā .. 4.6.190 ..
4.6.d:
देवासुराणां सर्वेषां मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम् ॥
तत्संप्राप्य कथाः कुर्यान्न गच्छेन्नरकं यथा ॥ 4.6.190 ॥
4.6.m: Human birth is exceedingly rare among all gods and asuras; / having attained it, one should recount tales so that one does not go to hell.

4.6.s:
svargāpavargalābhāya yadi nāsti samudyataḥ ..
svargasya mūlaṃ mānuṣyaṃ tadyatnādanupālayet .. 191 ..
4.6.d:
स्वर्गापवर्गलाभाय यदि नास्ति समुद्यतः ॥
स्वर्गस्य मूलं मानुष्यं तद्यत्नादनुपालयेत् ॥ 191 ॥
4.6.m: If one is not striving to attain heaven and final liberation, / [still,] human birth is the root of heaven: one should guard it with effort.

4.6.s:
dharmamūlena mānuṣyaṃ labdhvā sarvārthasādhakam ..
yadi lābhe na yatnaste mūlaṃ rakṣasva yatnataḥ .. 192 ..
4.6.d:
धर्ममूलेन मानुष्यं लब्ध्वा सर्वार्थसाधकम् ॥
यदि लाभे न यत्नस्ते मूलं रक्षस्व यत्नतः ॥ 192 ॥
4.6.m: Having obtained, by the capital of virtue, human birth which achieves all aims, / if you have no effort toward gain, guard the capital with care.

4.6.s:
manuṣyatve ca vipratvaṃ yaḥ saṃprāpyātidurllabham ..
na karotyātmanaḥ śreyaḥ konyastasmādacetanaḥ .. 193 ..
4.6.d:
मनुष्यत्वे च विप्रत्वं यः संप्राप्यातिदुर्ल्लभम् ॥
न करोत्यात्मनः श्रेयः कोन्यस्तस्मादचेतनः ॥ 193 ॥
4.6.m: And who is more senseless than he who, having attained / the exceedingly rare status of a brāhmaṇa within humanity, does not work for his own welfare?

4.6.s:
sarveṣāmeva deśānāṃ madhyadeśaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
ataḥ svargaśca mokṣaśca yaśaḥ saṃprāpyate naraiḥ .. 194 ..
4.6.d:
सर्वेषामेव देशानां मध्यदेशः परः स्मृतः ॥
अतः स्वर्गश्च मोक्षश्च यशः संप्राप्यते नरैः ॥ 194 ॥
4.6.m: Of all lands, the Middle Country is declared to be the best; / from here, heaven, liberation, and fame are attained by men.

4.6.s:
etasminbhārate puṇye prāpya mānuṣyamadhruvam ..
yaḥkuryādātmanaḥ śreyastenātmā rakṣitaḥ svayam ..
yaḥ kuryānnātmanaḥ śreyastenātmā vaṃcitaḥ svayam .. 195 ..
4.6.d:
एतस्मिन्भारते पुण्ये प्राप्य मानुष्यमध्रुवम् ॥
यःकुर्यादात्मनः श्रेयस्तेनात्मा रक्षितः स्वयम् ॥
यः कुर्यान्नात्मनः श्रेयस्तेनात्मा वंचितः स्वयम् ॥ 195 ॥
4.6.m: Having attained unsteady human birth in this sacred Bhārata, / he who works for his own welfare has protected his self by himself; / he who does not work for his own welfare has deceived his self by himself.

4.6.s:
bhogabhūmiḥ smṛtaḥ svargaḥ karmabhūmiriyaṃ matā ..
iha yatkriyate karma svarge tadupabhujyate .. 196 ..
4.6.d:
भोगभूमिः स्मृतः स्वर्गः कर्मभूमिरियं मता ॥
इह यत्क्रियते कर्म स्वर्गे तदुपभुज्यते ॥ 196 ॥
4.6.m: Heaven is declared to be the land of enjoyment; this is considered the land of action; / whatever action is done here is enjoyed in heaven.

4.6.s:
yāvatsvāsthyaṃ śarīrasya tāvaddharmaṃ samācara ..
asvasthaścātiyatnena na kiñcitkartumutsa het .. 197 ..
4.6.d:
यावत्स्वास्थ्यं शरीरस्य तावद्धर्मं समाचर ॥
अस्वस्थश्चातियत्नेन न किञ्चित्कर्तुमुत्स हेत् ॥ 197 ॥
4.6.m: As long as there is health in the body, so long practice dharma; / when unwell, even with great effort, one is not able to do anything.

4.6.s:
adhruveṇa śarīreṇa hyadhruvaṃ yaḥ prasādhayet ..
dhruvaṃ tasya paribhraṣṭamadhruvaṃ naṣṭameva ca .. 198 ..
4.6.d:
अध्रुवेण शरीरेण ह्यध्रुवं यः प्रसाधयेत् ॥
ध्रुवं तस्य परिभ्रष्टमध्रुवं नष्टमेव च ॥ 198 ॥
4.6.m: He who would accomplish the impermanent with an impermanent body, / has lost the permanent, and the impermanent is simply perished for him.

4.6.s:
āyuṣaḥ khaṃḍakhaḍāni nipataṃti tavā grataḥ ..
ahorātrāpadeśena kimarthaṃ nāvabudhyase .. 199 ..
4.6.d:
आयुषः खंडखडानि निपतंति तवा ग्रतः ॥
अहोरात्रापदेशेन किमर्थं नावबुध्यसे ॥ 199 ॥
4.6.m: Pieces of your lifespan are falling away before you / under the guise of days and nights; why do you not understand?

4.6.s:
yadā na jñāyate mṛtyuḥ kadā kasya bhaviṣyati ..
ākasmike hi maraṇe dhṛtiṃ viṃdeta kastadā .. 4.6.200 ..
4.6.d:
यदा न ज्ञायते मृत्युः कदा कस्य भविष्यति ॥
आकस्मिके हि मरणे धृतिं विंदेत कस्तदा ॥ 4.6.200 ॥
4.6.m: When it is not known when death will occur for whom, / who, then, could find fortitude in sudden death?

4.6.s:
parityajya yadā sarvamekākī yāsyasi dhuvam ..
na dadāsi tadā kasmātpātheyārthamidaṃ dhanam .. 201 ..
4.6.d:
परित्यज्य यदा सर्वमेकाकी यास्यसि धुवम् ॥
न ददासि तदा कस्मात्पाथेयार्थमिदं धनम् ॥ 201 ॥
4.6.m: When you will certainly depart alone, having abandoned everything, / why do you not give this wealth as provisions for the journey?

4.6.s:
gṛhītadānapātheyā sukhaṃ yāṃti mahādhvani ..
anyathā kliśyate jaṃtuḥ pātheyarahitaḥ pathi .. 202 ..
4.6.d:
गृहीतदानपाथेया सुखं यांति महाध्वनि ॥
अन्यथा क्लिश्यते जंतुः पाथेयरहितः पथि ॥ 202 ॥
4.6.m: Those who have taken the provisions of gifts travel happily along the great road; / otherwise, a creature travels along the path suffering, bereft of provisions.

4.6.s:
yeṣāṃ dvijendravāhitrī pūrṇabhāṃḍā tu gacchati ..
svargadeśasya pura tasteṣāṃ lābhaḥ padepade..203..
4.6.d:
येषां द्विजेन्द्रवाहित्री पूर्णभांडा तु गच्छति ॥
स्वर्गदेशस्य पुर तस्तेषां लाभः पदेपदे॥203॥
4.6.m: Those whose full vessel is carried by an eminent brāhmaṇa / ahead to the realm of heaven have gain at every step.

4.6.s:
iti jñātvā naraḥ puṇyaṃ kuryātpāpaṃ vivarjayet ..
puṇyena yāti devatvamapuṇyānnarakaṃ vrajet 204..
4.6.d:
इति ज्ञात्वा नरः पुण्यं कुर्यात्पापं विवर्जयेत् ॥
पुण्येन याति देवत्वमपुण्यान्नरकं व्रजेत् 204॥
4.6.m: Knowing this, a man should practice merit and avoid sin; / through merit one goes to godhood; through demerit one goes to hell.

4.6.s:
ye manāgapi deveśaṃ prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ śivam..
tepi ghoraṃ na paśyaṃti yamasya vadanaṃ narāḥ..205..
4.6.d:
ये मनागपि देवेशं प्रपन्नाः शरणं शिवम्॥
तेपि घोरं न पश्यंति यमस्य वदनं नराः॥205॥
4.6.m: Those men who take refuge in the lord of gods, Śiva, even in the slightest degree, / do not look upon the terrible face of Yama.

4.6.s:
kiṃ tu pāpairmahāghoraiḥ kiñcitkālaṃ śivājñayā.
.. bhavaṃti preta rājānastato yāṃti śivālayam.. 206..
4.6.d: किं तु पापैर्महाघोरैः किञ्चित्कालं शिवाज्ञया॥। भवंति प्रेत राजानस्ततो यांति शिवालयम्॥ 206॥
4.6.m: However, due to exceedingly terrible sins, by the command of Śiva they become / kings of pretas for a little while, and from there go to the abode of Śiva.

4.6.s:
ye punaḥ sarvabhāvena pratipannā maheśvaram ..
na te lipyaṃti pāpena padmapatramivāṃbhasā .. 207 ..
4.6.d:
ये पुनः सर्वभावेन प्रतिपन्ना महेश्वरम् ॥
न ते लिप्यंति पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवांभसा ॥ 207 ॥
4.6.m: Those, on the other hand, who have surrendered to Maheśvara with their whole being / are not smeared by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not by water.

4.6.s:
tasmā dvivardhayedbhaktimīśvare satataṃ budhaḥ ..
tanmāhātmyavicāreṇa bhavadoṣavirāgataḥ .. 208 ..
4.6.d:
तस्मा द्विवर्धयेद्भक्तिमीश्वरे सततं बुधः ॥
तन्माहात्म्यविचारेण भवदोषविरागतः ॥ 208 ॥
4.6.m: Therefore, the wise man should constantly increase his devotion to the Lord, / by reflecting on His majesty and by detachment from the flaws of worldly existence.

4.6.s:
pāpāni paṃca paramārthatayaiva pārtha duḥkhapradāni suciraṃ pitṛ rājaloke ..
anyāni yāni cirakālabhayānakāni vaktuṃ na yāṃti kila tāni parisphuṭāni .. 209 ..
śakaṭavratamāhātmyavarṇanam
4.6.d:
पापानि पंच परमार्थतयैव पार्थ दुःखप्रदानि सुचिरं पितृ राजलोके ॥
अन्यानि यानि चिरकालभयानकानि वक्तुं न यांति किल तानि परिस्फुटानि ॥ 209 ॥
शकटव्रतमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
4.6.m:
In ultimate truth, O Pārtha, the five sins bring sorrow for a very long time in the realm of the King of the Ancestors; / and the others that are terrifying for ages cannot indeed be fully described.
Description of the Greatness of the Cart Votive Observance

4.7.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
yadetatte samākhyātaṃ gaṃbhīraṃ narakārṇavama..
vratopavāsaniyamaplavenottīryate sukham .. 1 ..
4.7.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
यदेतत्ते समाख्यातं गंभीरं नरकार्णवम॥
व्रतोपवासनियमप्लवेनोत्तीर्यते सुखम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.7.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / That deep ocean of hell which has been described to you / is easily crossed by means of the raft of votive observances, fasts, and religious restraints.

4.7.s:
durllabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ vidyutpatanacañcalam ..
tathātmānaṃ samādadhyādbhraśyate na punaryathā .. 2 ..
4.7.d:
दुर्ल्लभं प्राप्य मानुष्यं विद्युत्पतनचञ्चलम् ॥
तथात्मानं समादध्याद्भ्रश्यते न पुनर्यथा ॥ 2 ॥
4.7.m: Having obtained a human birth, which is rare to attain and fleeting as the flash of lightning, / one should compose oneself in such a way that one does not fall again.

4.7.s:
dāna vratamayī kīrtiryasya syādiha dehinaḥ ..
paraloke'pi sa tayā jñāyate jñātivarddhanaḥ .. 3 ..
4.7.d:
दान व्रतमयी कीर्तिर्यस्य स्यादिह देहिनः ॥
परलोकेऽपि स तया ज्ञायते ज्ञातिवर्द्धनः ॥ 3 ॥
4.7.m: The fame of an embodied being in this world consisting of gifts and votive observances— / by that he is recognized even in the next world as one who elevates his kin.

4.7.s:
jñāyate neha nāmutra vratasvādhyāyavarjitaḥ ..
puruṣaḥ puruṣavyāghra tasmādvrataparo bhavet .. 4 ..
4.7.d:
ज्ञायते नेह नामुत्र व्रतस्वाध्यायवर्जितः ॥
पुरुषः पुरुषव्याघ्र तस्माद्व्रतपरो भवेत् ॥ 4 ॥
4.7.m: A man devoid of votive observances and sacred study is recognized neither here nor in the hereafter, / O tiger among men; therefore one should be devoted to votive observances.

4.7.s:
atra te kathayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam ..
siddhena saha saṃvādamavaṃtyāṃ brāhmaṇasya hi .. 5 ..
4.7.d:
अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् ॥
सिद्धेन सह संवादमवंत्यां ब्राह्मणस्य हि ॥ 5 ॥
4.7.m: Here I shall relate to you an ancient story: / the dialogue of a brāhmaṇa with a siddha in Avanti.

4.7.s:
yogarddhisiddhyā saṃsiddhaḥ kaścitsiddho mahītalam ..
cacāra vikṛtaṃ kṛtvā vapuḥ paramabhīṣaṇam .. 6 ..
4.7.d:
योगर्द्धिसिद्ध्या संसिद्धः कश्चित्सिद्धो महीतलम् ॥
चचार विकृतं कृत्वा वपुः परमभीषणम् ॥ 6 ॥
4.7.m: A certain siddha, perfected by the attainment of yogic power, roamed the earth, / having assumed a deformed and extremely terrifying body.

4.7.s:
nigīrṇadaṃto laṃboṣṭhaḥ piṃgākṣastanumūrddhajaḥ ..
truṭitaika karṇo durvaṇaḥ śīrṇavastro mahodaraḥ .. 7 ..
4.7.d:
निगीर्णदंतो लंबोष्ठः पिंगाक्षस्तनुमूर्द्धजः ॥
त्रुटितैक कर्णो दुर्वणः शीर्णवस्त्रो महोदरः ॥ 7 ॥
4.7.m: He had sunken teeth, pendulous lips, tawny eyes, sparse hair, / one severed ear, discoloured skin, ragged garments, and a large belly.

4.7.s:
cipiṭākṣaḥ sphuṭitapājjaṃghāḍhyaḥ kṛśakūrparaḥ ..
diśaḥ paśyati saṃhṛṣṭo babhrāmodbhrāṃtacittavat .. 8 ..
4.7.d:
चिपिटाक्षः स्फुटितपाज्जंघाढ्यः कृशकूर्परः ॥
दिशः पश्यति संहृष्टो बभ्रामोद्भ्रांतचित्तवत् ॥ 8 ॥
4.7.m: He had flat eyes, cracked feet, stout shanks, and emaciated elbows; / looking in all directions, he wandered about joyful like one whose mind is distracted.

4.7.s:
mūlajālikavipreṇa dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaśca ko bhavān ..
kadā svargātsamāyātaḥ kena kāryeṇa me vada .. 9 ..
4.7.d:
मूलजालिकविप्रेण दृष्टः पृष्टश्च को भवान् ॥
कदा स्वर्गात्समायातः केन कार्येण मे वद ॥ 9 ॥
4.7.m: He was seen by a brāhmaṇa who lived on root-fibres and asked, 'Who are you? / When did you come from heaven, and on what business? Tell me.

4.7.s:
kacciddṛṣṭā tvayā raṃbhā bhābhāsitadigaṃtarā ..
cittasaṃmohanakarī devānāmekasundarī .. 10 ..
4.7.d:
कच्चिद्दृष्टा त्वया रंभा भाभासितदिगंतरा ॥
चित्तसंमोहनकरी देवानामेकसुन्दरी ॥ 10 ॥
4.7.m: Have you seen Rambhā, who illumines the directions with her splendour, / who enchants the heart, the unique beauty among the gods?

4.7.s:
gatvā madvacanādvācyā nirvācyā doṣadarśibhiḥ ..
āvaṃtyastvāṃ kuśalinīṃ pṛcchati sma dvijo ttamaḥ .. 11 ..
4.7.d:
गत्वा मद्वचनाद्वाच्या निर्वाच्या दोषदर्शिभिः ॥
आवंत्यस्त्वां कुशलिनीं पृच्छति स्म द्विजो त्तमः ॥ 11 ॥
4.7.m: Having gone there, she, who is beyond censure by fault-finders, is to be spoken to on my behalf: / "An excellent brāhmaṇa of Avanti asks after your welfare."'

4.7.s:
siddhaḥ prasiddhaṃ taṃ vipraṃ prāhedaṃ vismayānvitaḥ ..
kathaṃ tvayāhaṃ vijñātaḥ svargādabhyāgataḥ sphuṭam .. 12 ..
4.7.d:
सिद्धः प्रसिद्धं तं विप्रं प्राहेदं विस्मयान्वितः ॥
कथं त्वयाहं विज्ञातः स्वर्गादभ्यागतः स्फुटम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.7.m: Filled with wonder, the siddha said to that renowned brāhmaṇa: / 'How was I recognized by you as clearly having arrived from heaven?'

4.7.s:
brāhmaṇastamathovāca vijñāto'si mayā yathā ..
tathā te'haṃ pravakṣyāmi kṣīṇāghaughāvadhāraya .. 13 ..
4.7.d:
ब्राह्मणस्तमथोवाच विज्ञातोऽसि मया यथा ॥
तथा तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि क्षीणाघौघावधारय ॥ 13 ॥
4.7.m: Then the brāhmaṇa said to him: 'How you were recognized by me, / that I shall declare to you; listen, O you whose heap of sins has dwindled!

4.7.s:
gātratrayaṃ virūpaṃ syāddvitīyaṃ vā svarūpataḥ..
dṛṣṭvā sarvāṃga vairūpyaṃ vijñāto'si tato mayā .. 14 ..
4.7.d:
गात्रत्रयं विरूपं स्याद्द्वितीयं वा स्वरूपतः॥
दृष्ट्वा सर्वांग वैरूप्यं विज्ञातोऽसि ततो मया ॥ 14 ॥
4.7.m: Three limbs might be deformed, or a second, by nature; / but having seen the deformity of all your limbs, you were thereby recognized by me.

4.7.s:
durllaṃghyā prakṛtiḥ sākṣādanubhūtakarī bhavet ..
prakṛteranyathābhāvaḥ sarvathā lakṣyate janaiḥ .. 15 ..
4.7.d:
दुर्ल्लंघ्या प्रकृतिः साक्षादनुभूतकरी भवेत् ॥
प्रकृतेरन्यथाभावः सर्वथा लक्ष्यते जनैः ॥ 15 ॥
